I read that passage last night and immediately closed the book and went to bed.
A refreshing approx. 487kcal pistachio lemon basil zucchini salad to improve sleep quality
피스타치오-레몬-바질-주키니-샐러드.ingredients: 1/2 zucchini, 1 clove garlic minced, parmesan cheese, (dressing) 2 [T] olive oil, 1/2 [T] honey, 1/4 cup chopped pistachios, 1/4 cup chopped basil, zest and juice of 1 lemon, a pinch of salt, a pinch of crushed pepper
피스타치오-레몬-바질-주키니-샐러드.steps:
1. Cut 1/2 zucchini into rough bite-sized pieces, sprinkle with salt, let sit about 15 minutes, then pat dry.
2. Meanwhile, mix 2T olive oil, 1/2T honey, 1/4 cup chopped pistachios, 1/4 cup chopped basil, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of crushed pepper thoroughly to make the dressing.
3. Heat olive oil in a pan, sauté the chopped garlic, then pan-fry the zucchini from step 1.
4. Plate the grilled zucchini, pour over the dressing from step 2, and top with parmesan cheese.

아보카도-들기름-두부면.title: Avocado Perilla Oil Tofu Noodles
아보카도-들기름-두부면.intro:
20251105 #breakfastdiary day 1552, 4°C/clear, 20min/exercise (M)
In an era of niche tastes, something needed 'for someone' rather than 'for everyone' (feat. today's long black, Monbell)
Approx. 513kcal avocado perilla oil tofu noodles
아보카도-들기름-두부면.ingredients: 1 pack thin tofu noodles, 1/2 avocado, 1T bonito flakes, (dressing) 2T tsuyu, 1T perilla oil, 1t sesame and black sesame seeds
아보카도-들기름-두부면.steps:
1. Rinse the tofu noodles under running water.
2. Halve the avocado, peel, and cut into 1cm pieces.
3. Mix 2T tsuyu, 1T perilla oil, 1t sesame and black sesame seeds to make the dressing.
4. Plate the tofu noodles, top with avocado and bonito flakes, and drizzle with the dressing from step 3.

오차즈케.title: Ochazuke
오차즈케.intro:
20251104 #breakfastdiary day 1551, 4°C/mostly clear
A day when I have to leave the house early for work. For today's ochazuke breakfast, I meant to steep kelp and bonito flakes last night before bed to make an umami-packed broth, but there was no kelp. Turning crisis into opportunity — I dug through the freezer and found 'the legendary megari broth-maker' and used that instead. Sure, tsuyu alone would be an easy shortcut, but today I wanted to do it a bit properly. Don't you have days like that, for no particular reason?
Over the megari broth, I added the yuzu-and-salmon soboro I bought over the weekend from @inseason_today #당유자연어소보로, making an approx. 250kcal ochazuke
오차즈케.ingredients: 1 pack omi rice, 1/2 pack furikake (bap-irang), 1T citron-salmon soboro, a little chives, (ochazuke broth) 5 megari, 2T bonito flakes, 2T tsuyu, 1/4t matcha
오차즈케.steps:
1. Before bed, add 500ml water and 5 megari to a pot and simmer for about 10 minutes, then remove the fish. Add 2T bonito flakes, boil for 1-2 minutes, turn off the heat, let sit for 5 minutes, then strain out only the broth.
2. In the morning, add 2T tsuyu and 1/4t matcha to the broth from step 1 and mix thoroughly. A delicious broth is complete.
3. In a mixing bowl, add the omi rice and 1/2 pack furikake and mix thoroughly.
4. Put the rice from step 3 in a bowl, pour over the broth from step 2, and top with the citron-salmon soboro and finely chopped scallion.

템페샐러드.title: #TempehSalad
템페샐러드.intro:
20251103 #breakfastdiary day 1550, -1°C/clear, 20min/exercise (M)
Romaine is torn by hand rather than cut with a knife, because cutting damages the leaf cells at the cut edge, making that part soggy and prone to oxidizing, which reduces the crisp texture and can make it wilt.
An approx. 350kcal #tempehsalad where my jaw dropped — the crunchy romaine paired with fried tempeh is the star of the show
템페샐러드.ingredients:
1 mini romaine, fried tempeh, cherry tomatoes and apple jujubes as much as you like, (dressing) 2T yogurt, 1t Dijon mustard, 1t white wine vinegar, salt, pepper

☝️For the fried tempeh: blend 3 cloves garlic, 1 red chili and 1/3 scallion, 5T starch, 50ml water, 1t salt, 1t dashida, 1t basil powder, 1/4t baking powder in a blender, then add the tempeh and fry.
템페샐러드.steps:
1. Tear the mini romaine into bite-sized pieces by hand.
2. Microwave yesterday's fried-chicken-style tempeh for 30 seconds, then cut in half.
3. Prep the cherry tomatoes and apple jujubes as well.
4. Mix 2T yogurt, 1t Dijon mustard, 1t white wine vinegar, salt, and pepper thoroughly.
5. In a bowl, combine the mini romaine, fried tempeh, cherry tomatoes and apple jujubes, and top with the dressing.

템페.title: Tempeh
템페.intro:
20251102 #breakfastdiary day 1549, 9°C/mostly clear
The original recipe calls for kaffir lime leaves and coriander powder, but I substituted perilla leaves and basil powder. Crispy outside, moist inside — Indonesian-style spicy #tempeh, fried
템페.ingredients: 1 tempeh, (batter) 3 cloves garlic, 1 red chili and 1/3 scallion, 5T starch, 50ml water, 1t salt, 1t dashida, 1t basil powder, 1/4t baking powder, (lemon mayo) 4T mayonnaise, 2T lemon juice, 1t whole grain mustard
템페.steps:
1. Tear the tempeh into rough bite-sized pieces by hand.
2. Make the batter. In a blender, blend 3 cloves garlic, 1 red chili and 1/3 scallion, 5T starch, 50ml water, 1t salt, 1t dashida, 1t basil powder, and 1/4t baking powder.
3. Add the tempeh to the batter from step 2, coat evenly, then pour oil into a pan and fry until golden.
4. Plate and serve with lemon mayo for dipping.

가지라자냐.title: #EggplantLasagna
가지라자냐.intro:
20251101 #breakfastdiary day 1548, 15°C/mostly clear
Eggplant lasagna made with leftover dumpling filling. With the eggplant pan-fried in olive oil, it's hard for this not to taste good — and since I skipped the tomato sauce, it ends up feeling more like a clear broth than a spicy stew.
Approx. 425kcal #eggplantlasagna
가지라자냐.ingredients: 1 eggplant, 2T mozzarella cheese, and (xiaolongbao) dumpling filling
가지라자냐.steps:
1. Slice the eggplant about 0.5cm thick, drizzle with olive oil, and pan-fry until golden. Eggplant soaks up a lot of oil.
2. Check on the dumpling filling left over from making xiaolongbao a few days ago. (sniff sniff) Seems still okay.
3. Line an oven dish with parchment paper and layer: fried eggplant, dumpling filling, mozzarella cheese, then fried eggplant, dumpling filling, mozzarella cheese again, and bake at 180°C for 10-20 minutes.
4. Plate and top with basil.

렌틸-커리-그리고-난.title: Lentil Curry and Naan
렌틸-커리-그리고-난.intro:
20251031 #breakfastdiary day 1547, 10°C/mostly cloudy
About 60% of the world's population uses tools like chopsticks, spoons, forks, and knives to eat. The remaining 40%, in a hand-eating culture found across India, other parts of South Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and some of Southeast Asia, use their hands instead of tools. That's more than you'd think. Anyway, if you trace the origin of the tools people use to eat, it's probably efficiency and utility that mattered more than taste or preference. Cutting food into manageable pieces, sometimes stabbing or picking it up — the main goal, one way or another, was getting food to the mouth as efficiently as possible.
(Najoshik, 'A Cultural History of Eating Utensils' from Everyday Breakfast)
Curry tastes best eaten by hand. A 631kcal lentil curry and naan, flavored with onion and tomato
렌틸-커리-그리고-난.ingredients: 5T lentils, 1/2 onion, 2 cloves garlic, 10 cherry tomatoes, 1 curry block, 1T balsamic vinegar, and naan
렌틸-커리-그리고-난.steps:
1. Soak the lentils in hot water for about 30 minutes.
2. Chop 1/2 onion and 2 cloves garlic. Prep the cherry tomatoes, removing the stems too.
3. Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté the garlic from step 1, then the onion. Add the tomatoes and sauté a bit more.
4. Pour in 600ml water, and once boiling, add 1 curry block and simmer for 2-3 minutes, then add the lentils from step 1 and simmer 2-3 minutes more. Turn off the heat, add today's twist — 1T balsamic vinegar — and mix thoroughly.

아보카도-토마토-버섯-세-가지-종류의-크로스티니-Crostini.title: Avocado, Tomato, and Mushroom — Three Kinds of Crostini
아보카도-토마토-버섯-세-가지-종류의-크로스티니-Crostini.intro:
20251030 #breakfastdiary day 1546, 7°C/mostly cloudy
Crostini is Italian for small, crispy bread. If bruschetta — topping a bigger piece of bread with tomato, basil, etc. — is closer to a simple meal, crostini uses a wider range of toppings beyond tomato and basil, like seafood, meat, and fruit, so... not quite a dessert, more like an appetizer.
Approx. 643kcal avocado, tomato, and mushroom — three kinds of crostini
아보카도-토마토-버섯-세-가지-종류의-크로스티니-Crostini.ingredients: 1/2 baguette, (No.1) 1T salsa sauce, 1/2 avocado, pepper and Maldon salt, (No.2) 1t lemon juice and olive oil, 2T ricotta cheese, 1T basil pesto, 3 cherry tomatoes, olive oil, salt, pepper, basil, (No.3) whipped ricotta cheese from No.2, 1 shiitake mushroom, pepper, parmesan cheese
아보카도-토마토-버섯-세-가지-종류의-크로스티니-Crostini.steps:
1. Slice the baguette 1cm thick, brush with olive oil, and toast until crisp.
2. No.1: spread salsa sauce on the baguette and top with sliced, well-ripened avocado. Add a little pepper and Maldon salt.
3. No.2: whip 1t lemon juice and olive oil into 2T ricotta cheese, spread on the baguette, then top with a little basil pesto and cherry tomatoes cooked with olive oil, salt, and pepper. A little balsamic would be nice too, but since this is the centerpiece, finish with basil instead.
3. No.3: top with the whipped ricotta from step 2 and thinly sliced shiitake mushroom. It's convenient to sauté the shiitake off to the side while cooking the cherry tomatoes in step 2. Finish with pepper and parmesan cheese.

가볍지만-진한-국물-들깨칼국수-사진에서-빛을-줄였더니-우울한-들깨칼국수가.title: Light but Rich Broth #PerillaSeedKalguksu — I turned down the brightness in the photo and it became a gloomy-looking perilla noodle soup.
가볍지만-진한-국물-들깨칼국수-사진에서-빛을-줄였더니-우울한-들깨칼국수가.intro:
20251029 #breakfastdiary day 1545, 5°C/clear, 20min/exercise (M)
But there's a more fundamental source of my dissatisfaction: 'light.' For posting, I photograph and film the finished breakfast, and 'light' has an absolute influence at that moment. Even at the same time of day, with the same breakfast, the light coming into the house varies hugely with the weather and season. So some days, a breakfast I'm genuinely happy with — the first in a while — ends up looking like the last breakfast from hell, while other days it looks like a warm, comforting bowl conjured by a mother's hands.
(Najoshik, 'Give Me Bright Light and Warm Sun' from Everyday Breakfast)

An approx. 230kcal light but rich-broth #perillaseedkalguksu made with tofu noodles
I turned down the brightness in the photo and it became a gloomy-looking perilla noodle soup.
가볍지만-진한-국물-들깨칼국수-사진에서-빛을-줄였더니-우울한-들깨칼국수가.ingredients: 2 shiitake mushrooms, 1/2 scallion, 1 pack tofu noodles, 3T ground perilla seeds, 1T tuna sauce (chamchiaek), 1 sheet lunchbox seaweed, 1t seafood dashida
가볍지만-진한-국물-들깨칼국수-사진에서-빛을-줄였더니-우울한-들깨칼국수가.steps:
1. Boil 600ml water and add the magic powder that gives a rich seafood-flavored broth.
2. Add 2 shiitake mushrooms, scallion, and the wide tofu noodles, and simmer about 5 more minutes.
3. Add ground perilla seeds and 1T tuna sauce, stir well, then ladle into a bowl. Just before eating, top with a sheet of lunchbox seaweed and a bit more ground perilla seeds.

샤오롱바오.title: #Xiaolongbao
샤오롱바오.intro:
20251028 #breakfastdiary day 1544, 2°C/clear, 20min/exercise (M)
Xiaolongbao (小笼包) means, in Chinese, a bao (bun/dumpling) steamed in a xiaolong ('small bamboo steamer'). Unlike regular dumplings, its defining feature is the hot broth/juice inside the filling. It's also a signature Shanghai dish. With xiaolongbao this large, the standard etiquette is to slurp the broth out with a straw first — hence the nickname '#StrawDumplings' at major tourist spots in Shanghai.
Instead of pork, I used shiitake mushroom, which somehow has a pork-like texture — though thinking about it, since I made the vegetable-stock jelly with gelatin (which is made from pork), it technically ends up being made with pork after all. Approx. 247kcal #xiaolongbao
샤오롱바오.ingredients: 5 shiitake mushrooms, 1/2 onion, 1/2 scallion (chopped), 1t soy sauce, 1T cooking wine, 1T oyster sauce, 1t garlic, 1t ginger, (vegetable stock jelly) 1/2 vegetable stock cube (Star Dado), 3 sheets leaf gelatin
샤오롱바오.steps:
1. Dissolve 1/2 vegetable stock cube in 200g boiling water. Add the leaf gelatin, pre-soaked for about 3 minutes, mix thoroughly, and set in the fridge overnight to firm up.
2. Chop 5 shiitake mushrooms, 1/2 onion, and 1/2 scallion, add 1t soy sauce, 1T cooking wine, 1T oyster sauce, 1t garlic, 1t ginger, and the vegetable-stock jelly (which will provide the 'broth'), and mix thoroughly.
3. Fill the dumpling wrappers with the xiaolongbao filling from step 2, seal completely, and steam for 10 minutes.
4. Take out of the steamer, poke in a straw to sip out the broth, then eat the dumpling.

땅콩호박샐러드.title: #ButternutSquashSalad
땅콩호박샐러드.intro:
20251027 #breakfastdiary day 1543, 8°C/clear
The butternut squash sat on my desk as a decorative object for about two weeks.
An approx. 390kcal #butternutsquashsalad served with pecans and ricotta cheese
땅콩호박샐러드.ingredients: 1/2 butternut squash, 2T pecans, 1T raisins, 2T ricotta cheese, 2T olive oil, salt, pepper, a little cinnamon, 1T honey
땅콩호박샐러드.steps:
1. Cut the butternut squash in half and cut into bite-sized pieces.
2. Place on a baking sheet, drizzle with 2T olive oil, sprinkle with salt, pepper, and cinnamon, mix thoroughly, and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes. Crumble the pecans in by hand and bake 5 minutes more.
3. Add 1T raisins, mix thoroughly, plate, and top with ricotta cheese. Finish with honey right before eating.

에그누들을-곁들인-걸쭉한-토마토-계란탕.title: Thick Tomato Egg Drop Soup with Egg Noodles
에그누들을-곁들인-걸쭉한-토마토-계란탕.intro:
20251026 #breakfastdiary day 1542, 12°C/mostly cloudy
10.23. On a business trip, and the whole breakfast video vanished, so it got skipped — now it's 10.26.
I'm back~🛬
The final episode of the ongoing Everyday Breakfast series, 'Rembrandt Lighting Doesn't Impress Me' (working title), is delayed. The ending is tough.
481kcal thick tomato egg drop soup with egg noodles
에그누들을-곁들인-걸쭉한-토마토-계란탕.ingredients: 1/3 scallion, 2 tomatoes, 1T fish sauce, 1/2 vegetable stock cube (Star Dado), 3 eggs, 25g egg noodles, 1T sesame oil
에그누들을-곁들인-걸쭉한-토마토-계란탕.steps:
1. Heat oil in a pot, cut and sauté 1/3 scallion, then add the cut tomatoes and sauté a bit more.
2. Add 600ml water, 1T fish sauce, and 1/2 vegetable stock cube (Star Dado), and simmer a bit longer.
3. Turn off the heat, beat in 3 eggs, and also stir in 1T starch dissolved in water.
4. Ladle the thick tomato egg soup from step 3 into a bowl, boil and cook 25g egg noodles in boiling water, and place on top. Finish with 1T sesame oil.

쉬림프볼-샐러드.title: Shrimp Ball Salad
쉬림프볼-샐러드.intro:
20251023 #breakfastdiary day 1541, 15°C/mostly clear
630kcal shrimp ball salad
Breakfast on hiatus for a few days due to a business trip.
쉬림프볼-샐러드.ingredients: 1 tomato, 1/2 red bell pepper, 1/2 yellow bell pepper, 1/4 onion, a little basil, 5 shrimp balls, 1T hemp seeds, (dressing) 3T olive oil, 1T white wine vinegar, 1T lemon juice, 1t whole grain mustard
쉬림프볼-샐러드.steps:
1. Prep the tomato, bell peppers, basil, and onion.
2. Boil the shrimp balls in boiling water, then cool in cold water.
3. Mix 3T olive oil, 1T white wine vinegar, 1T lemon juice, and 1t whole grain mustard thoroughly.
4. In a bowl, combine the vegetables from step 1, the shrimp balls, 1T hemp seeds, and the dressing from step 3, and mix well.

구운가지샐러드.title: #GrilledEggplantSalad
구운가지샐러드.intro:
20251022 #breakfastdiary day 1540, 6°C/mostly clear
It probably would've tasted even better coated in starch and deep-fried, but for health's sake I air-fried it instead and paired it with a tangy tomato dressing — 531kcal #grilledeggplantsalad
구운가지샐러드.ingredients: 2 eggplants, salt, starch, (dressing) 1 tomato, 1/4 onion, a little basil, 3T olive oil, 1T white wine vinegar, 1T lemon juice, 1T whole grain mustard
구운가지샐러드.steps:
1. Pound 2 eggplants and tear by hand, put in a zip bag with 2t salt and 2T starch, shake to coat, then air-fry at 180°C for 10 minutes. (Let it cool for about 5 minutes after air-frying for extra crispness.)
2. Chop 1 tomato and 1/4 onion, cut up a little basil, put in a mixing bowl, add 3T olive oil, 1T white wine vinegar, 1T lemon juice, and 1T whole grain mustard, and mix thoroughly.
3. Plate the eggplant from step 1 and drizzle with the dressing from step 2.

치크케이크.title: Cheesecake
치크케이크.ingredients: 170g Greek yogurt, 2 eggs, 30g oatmeal, 1T honey, 1t vanilla extract, a little blueberries
치크케이크.steps:
1. Pound 2 eggplants, tear by hand, and pan-fry in olive oil until nicely browned.
2. Chop 1 tomato and 1/4 onion, cut up a little basil, put in a mixing bowl, add 3T olive oil, 1T white wine vinegar, 1T lemon juice, 1T whole grain mustard, and 1T hemp seeds, and mix thoroughly.
3. Plate the eggplant from step 1 and drizzle with the dressing from step 2.

치즈-프리-블루베리-치즈케이크.title: Cheese-Free Blueberry Cheesecake
치즈-프리-블루베리-치즈케이크.intro:
20251021 #breakfastdiary day 1539, 8°C/mostly cloudy, 20min/exercise (M)
Since this is a cheesecake concept with no actual cheese, blending the oatmeal finely in a blender might work nicely for the texture.
I baked it at 180°C for 20 minutes, then raised it to 200°C for 15 more minutes. I think baking at 200°C for 20 minutes straight would be better. (Every oven's heat output differs, so keep an eye on it.)
An approx. 470kcal cheese-free blueberry cheesecake made with Greek yogurt and eggs
치즈-프리-블루베리-치즈케이크.ingredients: 170g Greek yogurt, 2 eggs, 30g oatmeal, 1T honey, 1t vanilla extract, a little blueberries
치즈-프리-블루베리-치즈케이크.steps:
1. In a mixing bowl, combine 170g Greek yogurt, 2 eggs, 30g oatmeal, 1T honey, and 1t vanilla extract, and mix thoroughly.
2. Line an oven dish with parchment paper, pour in the batter from step 1, add blueberries, and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes. After checking at 20 minutes it wasn't done, so I raised it to 200°C and baked 15 minutes more.

토마토-깻잎-비빔면.title: Tomato Perilla Leaf Bibim-myeon
토마토-깻잎-비빔면.intro:
20251020 #breakfastdiary day 1538, 6°C/partly cloudy, 20min/exercise (M)
Meanwhile, ancient Greeks and Romans are said to have eaten meals lying down. Special dining couches were arranged around the table. Each couch, called a triclinium (from the Greek 'kline,' meaning bed), could hold up to three men lying down. Each rested his head toward the table and leaned on his left elbow on a cushion. The hostess and other guests or attendants had to use chairs, and slaves had to remain standing the whole time.
(Bernd Brunner, The Art of Lying Down)
I thought — a whole book could be written just on the theme of 'lying down.' I briefly imagined eating breakfast lying down, but it doesn't seem workable.
A 360kcal tomato perilla leaf bibim-myeon made with soy milk noodles
토마토-깻잎-비빔면.ingredients: 1 pack soy milk noodles, 10 perilla leaves, 1 tomato, (dressing) 5T tsuyu, 1T perilla oil, 3T white wine vinegar, 7T water (adjust water to taste for seasoning)
토마토-깻잎-비빔면.steps:
1. Rinse the soy milk noodles under running water.
2. Roll up the perilla leaves and slice thinly. Cut the tomato and bell pepper into rough chunks too.
3. Put the soy milk noodles in a bowl and arrange the tomato, bell pepper, and perilla leaves around the edge.
4. Mix 5T tsuyu, 1T perilla oil, 3T white wine vinegar, and 7T water, and pour over.

콜리플라워-너깃.title: Cauliflower Nuggets
콜리플라워-너깃.intro:
20251019 #breakfastdiary day 1537, 14°C/mostly clear, 20min/exercise (M)
390kcal cauliflower nuggets
I used regular yogurt, which made the mixture too runny, so in the end it turned into more of a cauliflower omelet. Definitely use Greek yogurt.
콜리플라워-너깃.ingredients: 1/2 cauliflower, 1/3 cup yogurt, 1 egg, 1T olive oil, salt, pepper, paprika powder, (dip) 2T yogurt, 2T lemon juice
콜리플라워-너깃.steps:
1. Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized pieces and rinse under running water.
2. In a mixing bowl, combine 1/3 cup yogurt, 1 egg, 1T olive oil, salt, pepper, and paprika powder, then add the cauliflower from step 1 and mix.
3. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper, spread the cauliflower mixture from step 2, and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
4. Mix yogurt and lemon juice 1:1 for a dip and eat with that.

오트밀-말차-케이크.title: Oatmeal Matcha Cake
오트밀-말차-케이크.intro:
20251018 #breakfastdiary day 1536, 14°C/mostly clear
Still, what really determines whether a photo turns out well or poorly is light and sun. I usually eat breakfast and take photos around 7am, and as the days lengthen after the spring equinox, there's a higher chance of capturing a nice-feeling breakfast photo even at that hour, thanks to light coming through the window. Conversely, after the autumn equinox, when nights get longer, I have to rely on artificial lighting — so for breakfast photography, the spring and autumn equinoxes are a real crossroads of fortune. Of course, breakfast isn't only about light — sun matters too. One morning, the light falling on the mint I'd placed atop an apricot sandwich made the mint's green color pop even more, while the warm sun added a sense of vitality. That's what sunlight makes, and what sun does.
(Najoshik, 'Rembrandt Lighting Doesn't Impress Me' from Everyday Breakfast)
I'm polishing the final episode of #EverydayBreakfast, which started in July. When I do my year-end review in December, it'll likely take the double crown of both 'most embarrassing thing this year' and 'proudest thing this year.'
An approx. 570kcal oatmeal matcha cake that's just mixed together and microwaved for 3 minutes
오트밀-말차-케이크.ingredients: 90g oatmeal, 2g baking powder, 1T matcha, 1 egg, 150g soft tofu (sundubu), 20ml allulose, and pine nuts
오트밀-말차-케이크.steps:
1. In a bowl, first mix the oatmeal, soft tofu, baking powder, and matcha, then add the egg, soft tofu, and allulose, and mix thoroughly.
2. Line a bowl with parchment paper, pour in the batter from step 1, and microwave for 3 minutes.

오트밀-바나나-팬케이크.title: Oatmeal Banana Pancakes
오트밀-바나나-팬케이크.intro:
20251017 #breakfastdiary day 1535, 15°C/mostly clear, 20min/exercise (M)
An approx. 584kcal flour-free oatmeal banana pancake
오트밀-바나나-팬케이크.ingredients: 2 bananas, 3 eggs, 2T oatmeal, 1T Greek yogurt, coconut chips and cinnamon, olive oil
오트밀-바나나-팬케이크.steps:
1. Mash 1 banana finely, then mix in 3 eggs and 2T oatmeal thoroughly.
2. Coat a pan evenly with olive oil, lay slices of the other banana in, pour the batter from step 1 over, and cook on both sides.
3. Plate and top with cinnamon, 1T Greek yogurt, and coconut chips

가지수프.title: #EggplantSoup
가지수프.intro:
20251016 #breakfastdiary day 1534, 17°C/mostly cloudy
The original recipe calls for heavy cream, but I didn't have any, so I used milk and half a potato instead to make it thicker — approx. 300kcal #eggplantsoup
가지수프.ingredients: 2 eggplants, 1t butter, 1/2 potato, 1/2 onion, 2 cloves garlic, vegetable stock, 100ml milk, 300ml water, a little perilla leaves, 1t pine nuts
가지수프.steps:
1. Halve the eggplants, toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast in a 180°C oven for 30 minutes.
2. Meanwhile, melt butter in a pot and sauté finely chopped potato, minced onion, and minced garlic.
3. Pour 300ml water and the roasted eggplant from step 1 into the pot from step 2, add vegetable stock, simmer a bit more, then turn off the heat and blend with a hand blender.
4. Pour in a little milk and mix thoroughly. (Taste and season with salt.)
5. Plate and top the soup with pine nuts and chopped perilla leaves.

3분-두부-소면.title: 3-Minute Tofu Somyeon
3분-두부-소면.intro:
20251015 #breakfastdiary day 1533, 16°C/cloudy, 20min/exercise (M)
As I move the imagined recipe from my notes into reality, the second breakfast begins. This is when I actually prep and cook the ingredients according to what I wrote down, and taste the result. Unfortunately, it never turns out exactly as noted. The vegetable I meant to boil ends up blanched in hot water for one reason or another, and whether because of that or because it wasn't in the steamer long enough, once it's cooked it loses its shape and dissolves. So I chop it up and use it as a topping instead.
Some days I taste it and it's too salty, so I add a little water and taste again — now it's too bland. No, not quite that either — it's some weird, indescribable flavor. There's no time to start over from scratch, so I fix it with 1t chicken stock. An all-purpose cheat code. Of course, the deep flavor of the original ingredients is gone. It ends up tasting like broccoli eaten just for the chojang sauce, but it can't be helped. Anyway, that's how I end up eating breakfast twice in one day.
(Najoshik, 'Breakfast Is Basically Three Times a Day' from Everyday Breakfast)
☝️ Yesterday's freshly published episode (click the profile link~)
I made it with the recipe below but it didn't taste right — (everyone's palate differs, but) if I get the chance to make it again, I'll adjust it like this:
1 serving somyeon, 2T mashed tofu, 1t red chili flakes, 1T tsuyu, 2T fish sauce, 1T scallion, 1t sesame oil, and only 2.5 cups water,
put all the ingredients in a bowl, microwave for 3 minutes, and done — approx. 267kcal 3-minute tofu somyeon
3분-두부-소면.ingredients: 1 serving somyeon (thin wheat noodles), 2T mashed tofu, 1T red chili flakes, 1T soy sauce, 1T fish sauce, 1T scallion
3분-두부-소면.steps:
1. In a bowl, add the somyeon, 1T mashed tofu, 1T red chili flakes, 1T soy sauce, 1T fish sauce, 1T scallion, and 3 cups boiling water, and microwave for 3 minutes.
2. Done

순두부-계란찜-이랄까.title: Soft Tofu Steamed Egg, Sort Of?
순두부-계란찜-이랄까.intro:
20251014 #breakfastdiary day 1532, 15°C/cloudy, 20min/exercise (M)
I mixed about 30ml of milk into 2 eggs, but I think it's better not to. Whether because of that, or the thin pan, or not controlling the heat properly, or maybe all of it combined, the bottom got slightly burnt while the top stayed undercooked. Lucky-vicky. I ended up getting to enjoy quite a variety of flavors in one dish.
Approx. 320kcal soft tofu steamed egg, sort of?
순두부-계란찜-이랄까.ingredients: 1 soft tofu (sundubu), 2 eggs, 3 shrimp, a little scallion, salt, pepper
순두부-계란찜-이랄까.steps:
1. Place the soft tofu in a pan, cut it up roughly, then pour 2 beaten eggs over it. Add the shrimp, cover with a lid, and wait until cooked.
2. Plate and top with chili oil and scallion.

호박-프렌치토스트.title: Pumpkin French Toast
호박-프렌치토스트.intro:
20251013 #breakfastdiary day 1531, 17°C/drizzle, 20min/exercise (M)
So 'the first time making a breakfast' always comes with difficulty. Some days the taste and plating of the breakfast turn out exactly as I hoped, while other days it's bland and I have to grate in extra parmigiano reggiano to fix the seasoning, or the 'bomb' steamed egg doesn't explode the way I imagined, leaving me despairing in front of a deflated steamed egg. There are days the texture of chickpea hummus — chickpeas soaked overnight and blended — doesn't sit right with me, and I end up blaming the blender, thinking 'right, I should've bought that blender Starbucks supposedly uses.' Or the soufflé pancake, which I've never once nailed, gets blamed on this pan's uneven heat distribution, and I find myself browsing shopping sites for a pan with better heat conduction. Like the line from Between Calmness and Passion (2001) — not knowing 'when, and how much, to open your heart' — 'the first time making a breakfast' is always difficult, because I still don't quite know when and by how much to adjust the heat, the doneness of ingredients, and the seasoning.
(Najoshik, 'Lonely or Sad, I Still Have to Eat' from Everyday Breakfast)
I thought about making pumpkin purée, then bought a store-bought one instead and mixed it into milk — but it separates. Failed. I soaked rye bread in it and pan-fried it, and as expected, it separates too. Not the store-bought product's fault — I probably should've blended it finer and removed enough moisture. Learned something new today. Anyway, 462kcal pumpkin French toast
호박-프렌치토스트.ingredients: 3 slices rye bread, 200ml milk, 100g pumpkin purée, 1T maple syrup, a little cinnamon and vanilla extract, a little starch
호박-프렌치토스트.steps:
1. Mix 200ml milk, 100g pumpkin purée, 1T maple syrup, a little cinnamon and vanilla extract, and a little starch thoroughly.
2. Slice the rye bread 1cm thick and soak it well in the mixture from step 1.
3. Heat coconut oil in a pan and cook both sides until moist and golden.
4. Plate and top with cinnamon and ricotta cheese before eating.

옥수수쏨땀.title: #CornSomTam
옥수수쏨땀.intro:
20251012 #breakfastdiary day 1530, 17°C/cloudy, 20min/exercise (M)
Would've been even better with Thai yellow corn — approx. 400kcal #cornsomtam
옥수수쏨땀.ingredients: 1 corn, 3-4 green beans, 1-2 small tomatoes, 1 egg, 1t chopped peanuts, (can't quite call it a dressing, but:) 2 cloves garlic, 2-3 bird's eye chilies, 1t fish sauce, 1T lime juice, 1T coconut sugar, 3-4 slices tomato, 1T dried shrimp
옥수수쏨땀.steps:
1. Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 1-2 minutes.
2. Boil the egg. Soft-boiled or hard-boiled, either is fine.
3. Prep the tomato and corn.
4. In a mixing bowl, add 2 cloves chopped garlic, 2-3 bird's eye chilies, 1t fish sauce, 1T lime juice, 1T coconut sugar, 3-4 slices tomato, and dried shrimp, and pound gently.
5. Add the prepped green beans, tomato, and corn, and mix thoroughly.
6. Plate and top with a little chopped peanuts.

오트밀로-만든-당근-케이크.title: Oatmeal Carrot Cake
오트밀로-만든-당근-케이크.ingredients: 1 banana, 50g oatmeal, 1/2 carrot, 25g chopped pecans, 2T hemp seeds, 1/2t cinnamon, 1/2t baking powder, a pinch of salt, 200ml milk, (topping) Greek yogurt, honey, a little pecans
오트밀로-만든-당근-케이크.steps:
1. In an oven dish, mash 1 banana, then add 50g oatmeal, 1/2 shredded carrot, 25g chopped pecans, 2T hemp seeds, 1/2t cinnamon, 1/2t baking powder, a pinch of salt, and 200ml milk, and mix thoroughly.
2. Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.
3. Take out of the oven and top with Greek yogurt and pecans.
4. Cut into pieces, plate, and top with honey.

팟-크라파오-무-쌉-Phad-Krapow-Moo-Sap.title: Pad Krapow Moo Sap
팟-크라파오-무-쌉-Phad-Krapow-Moo-Sap.intro:
20251010 #breakfastdiary day 1528, 16°C/rain
Apparently there are now dedicated pad krapow moo sap places popping up in Bangkok. 'Pad' means stir-fried, 'krapow' means holy basil, 'moo' means pork, and 'sap' means minced — so what should I call this breakfast, made with tofu and perilla leaves instead of pork and holy basil?
1. Pad Perilla Leaf Tofu Sap
2. Pad Krapow Moo Sap made with tofu and perilla leaves
3. Whatever, really
An approx. 350kcal Pad Krapow Moo Sap made with tofu and perilla leaves
팟-크라파오-무-쌉-Phad-Krapow-Moo-Sap.ingredients: 1/2 block tofu, Thai basil seasoning paste, 1T black soy sauce, 4-5 perilla leaves, 1 egg, oil
팟-크라파오-무-쌉-Phad-Krapow-Moo-Sap.steps:
1. Microwave 1/2 block firm tofu for 2 minutes. Drain the water and crumble it by hand.
2. Heat oil in a pan, stir-fry the tofu from step 1, add the Thai basil seasoning paste and stir-fry a bit more, then add black soy sauce and chopped perilla leaves and stir-fry a bit longer.
3. In another pan with plenty of oil, fry 1 egg sunny-side up. The key for the egg on top of pad krapow moo sap is to fry it almost like deep-frying, with lots of oil.
4. Plate the tofu from step 2 and top with the egg from step 3.

핫도그.title: #HotDog
핫도그.intro:
20251009 #breakfastdiary day 1527, 22°C/cloudy
I've finally gone as far as microwaving carrots, pouring sauce over them, and glazing them down to look like sausages.
A 620kcal #hotdog with carrot instead of sausage
핫도그.ingredients: 2 small carrots, 1 hot dog bun, a little pickle, ketchup, mustard, (sauce) 3T olive oil, 3T white wine vinegar, 1T black soy sauce, 1t maple syrup
핫도그.steps:
1. Wash 2 small carrots, peel, wrap in plastic wrap, and microwave for 3 minutes.
2. In a pan, simmer the carrots from step 1 with 3T olive oil, 3T white wine vinegar, 1T black soy sauce, and 1t maple syrup. The carrots transform into something quite sausage-like.
3. Chop the pickle and set aside.
4. Heat olive oil in a pan and toast the hot dog bun.
5. Split the bun in half, add the carrot from step 2, top with the chopped pickle from step 3, and drizzle with ketchup and mustard.

크리스피-뇨끼.title: Crispy #Gnocchi
크리스피-뇨끼.intro:
20251008 #breakfastdiary day 1526, 23°C/clear
Gnocchi in a crispy parmesan-cheese coat
topped with basil pesto
and chopped perilla leaves
super-crunchy gnocchi
Long holiday, and doing dishes is such a hassle, so this is a one-pan meal — approx. 500kcal crispy #gnocchi
크리스피-뇨끼.ingredients: 2 cups gnocchi, parmesan cheese, olive oil, salt, 1T basil pesto, 2 perilla leaves
크리스피-뇨끼.steps:
1. Boil frozen gnocchi in salted boiling water until they float to the surface.
2. Add olive oil to a pan, add the gnocchi, and pan-fry, sprinkling parmesan cheese 2-3 times as you go. The gnocchi ends up with a crispy parmesan crust.
3. Top with a little basil pesto and finish with chopped perilla leaves and a bit more parmesan cheese.

비트샐러드.title: #BeetSalad
비트샐러드.ingredients: 1/2 beet, a little scallion, (marinade) 1T olive oil, 3T white wine vinegar, 1t maple syrup, (dressing) 1T peanut butter, 1T lemon juice, 1t maple syrup
비트샐러드.steps:
1. Wash the beet thoroughly, cut into wedges, and boil for 30 minutes or more.
2. In a mixing bowl, add the beet along with 1T olive oil, 3T white wine vinegar, and 1t maple syrup, and mix thoroughly. Marinate for 30 minutes.
3. Plate the beet, mix 1T peanut butter, 1T lemon juice, and 1t maple syrup thoroughly, and spoon over the beet. Top with sliced scallion.

포멜로.title: Pomelo
포멜로.intro:
20251005 #breakfastdiary day 1524, 28°C/partly cloudy
I made a pomelo salad using the Pian Kan Pomelo kit from @yoiyoii.recipe, which I happened to come across. (It's a recipe that actually won the top prize at a regional competition.)
Nakhon Pathom has a small, pretty dessert café, so if I ever get the chance I'd like to visit and try Thailand's traditional and fusion desserts. Nakhon Pathom is about an hour from Bangkok and is well known as a region producing high-quality pomelo.
포멜로.ingredients: Pomelo, shallots and lemongrass, mint, palm sugar, fried garlic, sweet-and-spicy fish sauce (not sure of the exact recipe, but it seems to have palm sugar, fish sauce, chopped chili, lime juice, etc. — very sweet and very spicy.)
포멜로.steps:
1. Mix together the boxed pomelo, shallots and lemongrass, mint, palm sugar, fried garlic, and the sweet-and-spicy fish sauce.
2. Line a plate with banana leaf, put the pomelo salad from step 1 into a krathong (a small crispy shell/basket), and garnish with mint and butterfly pea.

포멜로새우샐러드.title: #PomeloShrimpSalad
포멜로새우샐러드.intro:
20251004 #breakfastdiary day 1523, 28°C/cloudy, 30min/exercise (W, M)
Peeling pomelo is always such a chore, so being able to get pomelo already peeled — outer skin and inner membrane both — is amazing. Approx. 165kcal #pomeloshrimpsalad
포멜로새우샐러드.ingredients: 1/2 pomelo, 3 shrimp, a little cilantro, (dressing) 1/2 stalk lemongrass, 1 shallot, lime juice (juice of 1 lime), 1T coconut sugar, 1T fish sauce
포멜로새우샐러드.steps:
1. Peel the outer skin and inner membrane off 1/2 pomelo.
2. Score the backs of the shrimp and blanch in boiling water.
3. Pound 1/2 stalk of lemongrass, then chop finely.
4. Thinly slice 1 shallot.
5. In a mixing bowl, combine the lemongrass from step 3, the shallot from step 4, lime juice, 1T coconut sugar, and 1T fish sauce, and mix thoroughly.
6. In a mixing bowl, combine the pomelo, shrimp, cilantro, and chopped peanuts, mix thoroughly, and plate.

태국식아침디저트-디저트.title: Thai-Style Breakfast Dessert
태국식아침디저트-디저트.ingredients: Egg, banana, purple sweet potato, etc.
태국식아침디저트-디저트.steps:
1. Fold a banana leaf and secure it with a skewer, then crack an egg into it. Cook slowly over low heat.
2. Also grill the banana and purple sweet potato slowly over low heat.
3. Line a plate with banana leaf and arrange the fried egg from step 1, grilled banana, and purple sweet potato. Serve with a little honey on the side.

까이끄라타.title: #KaiKrata
까이끄라타.intro:
20251001 #breakfastdiary day 1521, 25°C/localized heavy downpour
A pro breakfast-eater's baseline for a breakfast made by someone else is meat, at minimum ✌️
Kai krata — 'kai' means egg, 'krata' means pan — literally, egg cooked in a pan, and a signature breakfast of Thailand's northern and northeastern (Isan) regions.
Given the geography, it's no surprise Chinese and Laotian food culture shows through (is there anywhere that isn't shaped by its neighbors?) — sure enough, the red sausage is Chinese-style, sweeter and saltier than the rest. And of course there's also a paler traditional Thai-style sausage, filled with sticky rice instead of starch — also distinctive.
Today's breakfast wasn't homemade, but still, approx. 520kcal #kaikrata
까이끄라타.ingredients: 2 eggs, a little Thai sausage, 2T minced pork, oil, soy sauce, fish sauce, salt, pepper, chopped chives
까이끄라타.steps:
1. Heat oil in a pan, add 1t soy sauce, 1t fish sauce, salt, and pepper, and stir-fry the minced pork.
2. Cut the Thai sausage into suitable pieces and pan-fry.
3. Fry 2 eggs sunny-side up.
4. In a small pan, arrange the sunny-side-up eggs from step 3, the sausage from step 2, and the fried pork from step 1, warm briefly, and add chives and pepper.

포카치아피자.title: #FocacciaPizza
포카치아피자.intro:
20250927 #breakfastdiary day 1520, 21°C/clear, 20min/exercise (M)
People scold an indecisive person by saying they're 'like water mixed with water, liquor mixed with liquor.' Every time I hear that phrase, I sense a positive nuance hiding behind its negative surface. I actually like people who are 'like water in water, liquor in liquor' (I even envy them). Even if to others they seem to lack decisiveness, seem 'wishy-washy,' or 'bland,' they hold onto their true nature regardless.
(Kim Jin-hae, Like Water Mixed With Water)
I read this in the paper yesterday and liked it enough to jot it down.
Topped with spicy salsa sauce and cheese and baked once more, but its true nature remains intact — 340kcal #focacciapizza
포카치아피자.ingredients: 1 piece focaccia, 1T salsa sauce, 1T mozzarella cheese, 2-3 cherry tomatoes, a little basil powder, 1T ricotta cheese, 1T olive oil
포카치아피자.steps:
1. Slice the focaccia horizontally. If you prefer a thicker crust, leave it unsliced.
2. Spread salsa sauce on the focaccia, top with mozzarella cheese and small pieces of cherry tomato. Sprinkle a little basil powder and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes. (Just enough for the mozzarella to melt.)
3. Plate the focaccia, drizzle with olive oil, top with whipped ricotta cheese and basil, and finish with olive oil.

별일이-없으면-날마다-어제와-다른-조식을-만들어-먹는다-이-말에는-우.title: 20250926 #breakfastdiary day 1519, 20°C/cloudy
별일이-없으면-날마다-어제와-다른-조식을-만들어-먹는다-이-말에는-우.intro:
20250926 #breakfastdiary day 1519, 20°C/cloudy
'If nothing comes up, I make and eat a different breakfast every day from the day before' — this statement comes with a condition: 'if nothing comes up.' That 'something' means being too sick to eat breakfast, or being away from the kitchen for a business trip or travel. Of course, on a smaller scale, there's also the once-a-year health checkup day, when I fast and skip breakfast.
(Najoshik, 'Lonely or Sad, I Still Have to Eat' from Everyday Breakfast)
