토스트-2.title: Toast
토스트-2.intro:
20231220, #breakfastdiary 927, -9°C/partly cloudy
Rise up on your toes
and make room
for the first snow to land
(Lee Won, 'This Is a Love Song')
Cold and snowing, so public transit will be packed and the commute rough — I take a deep breath 🧘‍♂️ and make a little room in my mind, too. 
Brush both sides of the bread with olive oil and toast it in a pan. 
Spread on basil pesto, top with a sunny-side-up egg, and finish with a light shake of seasoning
Everything but the bagel sesame seasoning 👍

양파수프-양파-2.title: Onion Soup
양파수프-양파-2.intro:
20231219, #breakfastdiary 926, -7°C/partly cloudy
The days of setting KPIs around customer loyalty are over. Are they, really? 
Slice 2 onions and sauté in a buttered pan. Add a little salt and keep sautéing. And sautéing. Look away for a second and it burns. 
Transfer to a pot, pour in wine, and simmer briefly just to cook off the alcohol. 
Add water and 1T chicken stock, and bring to a rolling boil. 
Ladle into a pot, top with two slices of bread and a generous heap of parmesan, and (after a moment's hesitation between the air fryer and the oven) torch it 🔥

넷플릭스-나디야의초간단레시피-라즈베리크림치즈크로와상.title: Raspberry Cream Cheese Croissant (Nadiya's Quick Recipes, Netflix)
넷플릭스-나디야의초간단레시피-라즈베리크림치즈크로와상.intro:
20231218, #breakfastdiary 925, 0°C/mostly clear, 20 min/workout (T) 
Croissants filled with fresh(?) frozen raspberries mixed with ricotta and baked until wonderfully crisp 🥐
Raspberries are a not-too-distant cousin of our native wild raspberries. This filling turned out less sweet than I expected — I almost wondered if I should've added more sugar — but apparently raspberries are naturally more tart than sweet to begin with. It's a tart-more-than-sweet kind of flavor. 
Mix 150g ricotta cheese (one whole tub), 1 sugar, a splash of vanilla extract, and a cup of raspberries until evenly combined. The color is genuinely gorgeous. Add 1T all-purpose flour and half an egg, mix a bit more, and the filling is done. 
Split store-bought croissants in half, press them into a muffin tin, and fill with the prepared filling. Bake for 10 minutes in a 180°C oven.

구포간장국수-간장국수.title: Gupo Soy Sauce Noodles
구포간장국수-간장국수.intro:
20231217, #breakfastdiary 924, -9°C/mostly clear, 20 min/workout (Y) 
Gupo noodles originated in Busan's Gupo Market, and after a court ruled that no single business could monopolize a name that's essentially a local specialty, almost every noodle maker in Busan started using the 'Gupo noodles' name. Not quite the same story, but it reminds me a bit of how 'Kimbap Heaven' became a generic name too. 
Mix 4 soy sauce, 2 sesame oil, 2 sugar, and 0.5 minced garlic well to make a dressing. 
Boil the noodles and rinse thoroughly in cold water. Plate the noodles, top with an egg yolk, chopped chives, sesame seeds, and drizzle with the dressing.

핫도그-2.title: Hot Dog
핫도그-2.intro:
20231216, #breakfastdiary 923, -5°C/windy
We call this affliction boredom, the feeling that life is meaningless, the sense that an abundant yet joyless life is slipping through your fingers like sand, the bewildered feeling of not knowing where to go or what to do. The French gave it a name, but we never did. We only got our own name for it fairly recently. We call this affliction 'neurosis.'
@longblack.co Why do I keep falling back into this listlessness
When I feel listless, I don't overthink it — I just do something. Doing it is how you figure it out. 
A pre-pandemic, one-dollar hot dog from a food truck near St. Lawrence Avenue in the Bronx, New York 
Melt a knob of butter in a pan and warm the bun on both sides. 
(Casually, as if it's nothing) Top the bun with ketchup, mustard, and sriracha, then add chopped tomato and onion.

무조림을곁들인온메밀-온메밀.title: Warm Buckwheat Noodles with Braised Radish
무조림을곁들인온메밀-온메밀.intro:
20231214, #breakfastdiary 922, 7°C/drizzle, 21 min/workout (Y) 
A warm, brothy breakfast I made expecting a chilly morning — #warmbuckwheatnoodleswithbraisedradish 
Turns out I was wrong about the weather 👍
Fill a pot with plenty of water and add kelp and shiitake mushrooms, then bring to a boil. Once it boils, turn off the heat, remove the kelp and mushrooms, and add bonito flakes. Let it sit quietly for a bit, then strain out the bonito flakes. (A dashi broth made because I had the time for it) 
Pour about 850ml of the dashi into a pot, add 1T each of soy sauce, tsuyu, and oligo syrup, and braise the radish down (it's ready after about the length of a 20-minute yoga session). 
Pour 200ml of stock into the dashi used for braising the radish, add 1 soy sauce and 1 oligo syrup, and bring to a gentle simmer. 
Boil the buckwheat noodles, rinse in cold water, plate with the mushrooms and radish, and pour over the broth you just made. 
Recipe from @sogumgooi.

표고버섯-표고버섯파스타-파스타.title: Shiitake Mushroom Pasta
표고버섯-표고버섯파스타-파스타.intro:
20231213, #breakfastdiary 921, 1°C/mostly clear
Before my #shiitakemushrooms wilt any further, a #shiitakemushroompasta built entirely around them
Trim the stems off 5 shiitake mushrooms and wipe the caps clean with a paper towel. Cut 2 into big chunks and finely chop the other 3. 
Heat a generous amount of olive oil in a pan and cook the mushrooms. Once they've soaked up enough oil and look ready, add minced garlic and peperoncino (seeds removed). 
When the pot of water boils, add the pasta, cook for 2-3 minutes, then drain and add it to the pan with the mushrooms along with some pasta water, and simmer. Once the pasta water has reduced, add salt, mantecare it together, and plate. 
*Reference recipe from the YouTube channel Jun's Bistro.

베러미트-쿠스쿠스샐러드-식물성대체육.title: Couscous Salad with Plant-Based Meat
베러미트-쿠스쿠스샐러드-식물성대체육.intro:
20231212, #breakfastdiary 920, 4°C/cloudy, 21 min/workout (L)
To #BetterMeat — it's debatable, sure, but they say it's 100% plant-based with no sodium nitrite or animal fat, so surely it's earned a seat at the table alongside the other vegetables in this salad? 🤔
Soak 100g couscous in 100g water. 
Cut up the Better Meat and add it along with tomato, apple, onion, olives, and cucumber, then mix in olive oil, salt, salt, pepper, pepper, and lemon juice, and toss well. 
Plate it and top with a few mint leaves. 
Reference recipe from @leplat_pmj. 
#

길거리토스트-시애틀핫도그-핫도그.title: Seattle-Style Hot Dog (Street Toast Style)
길거리토스트-시애틀핫도그-핫도그.intro:
20231211, #breakfastdiary 919, 9°C/cloudy, 21 min/workout (Y)
It's already been a few years since #streettoast made it into the New York Times as a signature Korean street food. In the same vein (though this news is a bit old too), Korean-style hot dogs have become quite popular abroad as well. The secret to that popularity is said to lie in the sheer variety of ingredients and sauces used. 
Actually, American hot dogs vary a lot by region too, each with its own signature ingredients and sauces. And of course, within any one region, personal taste produces all kinds of combinations. 
Seattle-style hot dogs oddly include cream cheese, and even after searching around and asking ChatGPT, I never did find out why. 
Sauté onion thoroughly with salt and pepper (usually called caramelized onion) and set aside. 
Split the sausage lengthwise and air-fry for 5 minutes. 
Meanwhile, split the hot dog bun in half and toast in a buttered pan. (Oh no, burnt it again) 
Spread the bun generously with cream cheese, then top with the sausage, the well-sautéed onion, sauerkraut, and a good squeeze of sriracha~ 
Better than it looks — a proper Seattle-style hot dog

콩고기-대체육-비욘드미트.title: 'Bean Meat?' — Alternative Meat
콩고기-대체육-비욘드미트.intro:
20231210, #breakfastdiary 918, 5°C/cloudy, 21 min/workout (U)
'Alternative meat? Oh, that? #beanmeat?' 
That used to be the typical reaction to #alternativemeat. It mimicked the texture and aroma of real meat, but fell well short of expectations — though the category has come a long way in just the past few years. 
Overseas, #BeyondMeat and #ImpossibleFoods have already been supplying alternative meat to chains like KFC and Burger King for years, and domestically, companies like Shinsegae Food and Pulmuone are expanding the market too — not just the alternative meat itself, but restaurants built around it. 
Microwave Shinsegae Food's #luncheonkimchiricebowl for 2 minutes 30 seconds. Even though it already comes with a slice of luncheon meat, I slice up a piece of #plantbasedluncheonmeat, pan-fry it, and add it on top anyway. 
Of course it's tasty just like that, but after a bite with the chopped chives and luncheon meat, I remember the sesame oil I forgot to add, and stir that in too.

만두.title: Dumplings
만두.intro:
20231209, #breakfastdiary 917, 10°C/mostly cloudy
I zoned out for just a moment and burned it. At least it was the dumplings and not my peace of mind, so I'll call that a win. 
Heat oil in a pan and pan-fry the dumplings. Once they're cooked through, pour in a starch slurry (1T starch to half a cup of water), scatter on plenty of chives, lower to a simmer, cover, and leave for about 10 minutes until the slurry reduces down.

중국식토마토스크램블에그-토마토-스크램블.title: Chinese-Style Tomato Scrambled Eggs
중국식토마토스크램블에그-토마토-스크램블.intro:
20231208, #breakfastdiary 916, 9°C/mostly clear, 21 min/workout (Y)
With ketchup and corn starch added for extra tang, a brighter look, and a creamy finish — a proper #Chinesestyletomatoscrambledeggs
Finely chop chives, onion, and tomato, and prep 2 beaten eggs with salt and pepper. 
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the chopped onion until translucent. 
Add the chopped cherry tomatoes and sauté, then stir in 1T ketchup, 1t sugar, 1T water, plus a mixture of 2T water with 1t corn starch, pour it in, simmer a bit longer, and set aside in a bowl. 
Heat oil in a pan, add salt and pepper to the beaten eggs, pour them in, and stir. Right at the moment you're unsure whether the eggs are cooked or not, turn off the heat, pour in the tomato mixture, and mix evenly. Finish with the chopped chives~
Oh, and this is meant to be eaten over rice, like a rice bowl. 
Recipe from KP Kwan's YouTube channel, #TasteofAsianFood. 
Just adding this one thing changes tomato scrambled eggs completely — #Chinesestyletomatoscrambledeggs

팬케이크.title: Pancakes
팬케이크.intro:
20231207, #breakfastdiary 915, 1°C/clear
Even with a store-bought pancake mix, or a product like the one I had today where you just add water or milk and shake to make the batter, pancakes are (if you want to do it right) actually a surprisingly demanding breakfast that calls for careful heat control and a fair bit of patience.
It's a bit like casting a line into a still lake and sitting there blankly, and when someone passing by asks 'what are you fishing for,' instead of answering 'oh, just fishing for time,' you could just as naturally say 'oh, just cooking pancakes' — that kind of feeling. That's what crossed my mind while pouring batter into the pan and zoning out. 
Over gentle heat, add oil and coat the pan with a paper towel. Leave it be for about 5 minutes. 
Pour water into the store-bought pancake mix, shake it up, ladle a scoop onto the pan, and wait patiently. Just as your patience is about to run out, flip it and wait through another stretch of patience. That's how you finally get one finished pancake. 
Top with a knob of butter and a generous pour of maple syrup for extra moistness and sweetness~

어묵탕-어묵-오뎅.title: Fish Cake Soup (Eomuk-tang)
어묵탕-어묵-오뎅.intro:
20231206, #breakfastdiary 914, 4°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(L) 
Pour 700ml of water into a pot and add the powdered soup packet that comes with the store-bought fish cakes. The broth is already worldly-perfect on its own, but for a little extra depth I add a big chunk of radish and some shiitake mushrooms and (🎱🎱) let it simmer. (The water made it a bit bland, so I added 2T of tsuyu.) 
Skewer the fish cakes on sticks, drop them into the pot, and blanch for about 5 minutes. 
In a bowl, arrange crown daisy greens, shiitake mushrooms, a boiled egg, and the fish cakes, then pour in the broth.

쑥갓두부샐러드-김대석셰프-두부.title: Crown Daisy and Tofu Salad
쑥갓두부샐러드-김대석셰프-두부.intro:
20231205, #breakfastdiary 913, 1°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/workout(Y) 
I was reminded again that the same ingredients become a side dish when tossed, and a main dish when stacked up. 
Ingredients: 270g crown daisy greens (1t sea salt for blanching), 1 block tofu, 1/3t minced garlic, 1/3t salt, 1/2t soy sauce, 1/2 sesame oil, 1T black sesame seeds, 10 peanuts
(Ingredients from a YouTube recipe by #chefkimdaeseok.) 
Add salt to boiling water and blanch crown daisy greens cut into 3cm pieces. Rinse in cold water and squeeze out the moisture. 
Blanch the tofu in the same water used for the greens for about 1 minute. 
On a plate, arrange the crown daisy greens and mash the tofu on top, then add the dressing, black sesame seeds, and chopped peanuts. Toss gently and enjoy. 
(If you're not tossing it, you could probably skip the garlic.)

카이찌여우-더쿡-태국오믈렛.title: Thai Omelette (Kai Jeow)
카이찌여우-더쿡-태국오믈렛.intro:
20231204, #breakfastdiary 912, -5°C/clear, 21min/workout(U) 
A Thai-style omelette, #kaijeow
According to #thecook, if there's a scale for how intense omelette cooking gets, French omelettes sit at the far left, American omelettes a bit further right, and all the way at the right end is the Thai omelette, kai jeow. 
Anyway, anything deep-fried can hardly taste bad, but what really gets me is the edges — those airy, ready-to-fly-away layers that are somehow crispy at the same time. #soyummy
First, mix 2T sriracha sauce, 1/2t fish sauce, 1t oligo syrup, and 1T lime juice to make the dressing. 
Beat 2 eggs with 1/2t fish sauce until well combined. (Really mix it well.) Pour plenty of oil into a wok, heat until it just starts to smoke, then pour in the beaten eggs. 
After about 30 seconds — once you've checked the bottom has set — carefully flip it so the oil doesn't splatter. Another 30 seconds later, check the bottom again, shake off a little oil over the pan, and quickly flip it onto the rice. 
Pour over the sriracha dressing (cilantro would be great here, but I didn't have any) and top with chopped scallions.

양배추스테이크-양배추.title: Cabbage Steak
양배추스테이크-양배추.intro:
20231203, #breakfastdiary 911, 4°C/clear
Every time I opened the fridge, that awkward leftover bit of cabbage had been bugging me for over a week, so I finally just used it up. 
Ingredients: cabbage, soy dressing (2 soy sauce, 2 cooking wine, 1 sugar, 0.5 garlic, 1/2 cup water), scallions (optional) 
Heat oil in a pan and lay the cabbage in. Sear both sides once, drizzle with the soy dressing, and sear both sides again. Once the cabbage turns tender, move it to a plate, drizzle with the remaining dressing, and top with scallions. 
A really simple #cabbagesteak

호두와쑥갓을곁들인안초비감자샐러드-감자크로켓-감자.title: Potato Croquettes
호두와쑥갓을곁들인안초비감자샐러드-감자크로켓-감자.intro:
20231202, #breakfastdiary 910, 3°C/mostly cloudy
I chopped up the leftover #walnutandcrowndaisyanchovypotatosalad from yesterday, coated it in egg and breadcrumbs, and baked it in the air fryer at 180°C for 10 minutes on each side. 
Mayo and ketchup are nice, but for fried food, sriracha still wins. #potatocroquettes

그럴수록요리-감자-안초비.title: Anchovy Potato Salad with Walnuts and Crown Daisy
그럴수록요리-감자-안초비.intro:
20231201, #breakfastdiary 909, -7°C/clear, 21min/workout(Y) 
This is the walnut and crown daisy anchovy potato salad recipe from the essay #themoresoicook, though I changed the amounts and order a bit. The recipe says to mash the potatoes first and then add the onion and crown daisy, but I find it easier to mix in liquids like butter, mayo, and yogurt first before folding in the rest. Turns out this dish works your forearms more than you'd expect, 💪
Ingredients: 3 potatoes, 1/2 onion, 2 stalks crown daisy, 1T butter, 2 anchovies, a small handful of walnuts, 2T mayo, 1T yogurt, plus salt and pepper
Boil the potatoes with the skin on, then peel while hot and mash. 
Mix in the anchovies, mayo, and yogurt evenly, then fold in the onion, crown daisy, and walnuts — adding the anchovies and tasting as you salt is best. A little pepper and some of the (leftover) anchovy oil rounds out the flavor nicely. 
Mound it generously on a plate and finish with scallions and a walnut piece

오이샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드-오이.title: Cucumber Salad
오이샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드-오이.intro:
20231130, #breakfastdiary 908, -7°C/clear
Ingredients: 1 cucumber, 4 radishes, 1/4 onion, 2T pumpkin seeds, vinaigrette (3T olive oil, 1T white wine vinegar, 1t whole grain mustard) 
Slice the cucumber and radishes on a mandoline. Slice the onion and soak it in water ahead of time. Lightly toast the pumpkin seeds in a pan. 
In a bowl, combine the cucumber, radishes, onion, and pumpkin seeds, drizzle with the vinaigrette, and toss evenly. Really simple. 
From the #mylocalfoodsalad recipe.

앤초비파스타-맛수령-파스타.title: Anchovy Pasta
앤초비파스타-맛수령-파스타.intro:
20231129, #breakfastdiary 907, -4°C/mostly cloudy, 20min/workout(L) 
After losing my sense of smell to COVID last year, I figured now was the perfect time (since I wouldn't have to fight through the fishy smell) to finally make anchovies myself, so I bought 1kg of fresh anchovies, cured them, and even made pasta with them — but it turned out less tasty than I'd hoped. There are several reasons for that, which I'll sort out another time, but for now: let's just buy anchovies. They're cheap and delicious. 
Ingredients: 3 cloves garlic, 2 cherry tomatoes, 3-4 anchovies, about 10 capers, butter (adds an explosion of flavor🌋, optional), pasta, salt
Since this is an oil-based pasta, heat plenty of olive oil in a pan and sauté or gently poach the capers and anchovies over low heat. Add the garlic and tomatoes. 
Add the pasta and a cup of pasta water, stir well, and once it's cooked through, turn off the heat, add a knob of butter, and mantecare by stirring vigorously before plating. Enjoy~
*Recipe from the YouTube channel #matsuryeong. 
-
20231129, #breakfastdiary 907, -4°C/mostly cloudy, 20min/workout(L) 
Ingredients: 3 cloves garlic, 2 cherry tomatoes, 3-4 anchovies, about 10 capers, butter (adds an explosion of flavor🌋, optional), pasta, salt

*Recipe from the YouTube channel #matsuryeong.

모듬콩샐러드-콩.title: Mixed Bean Salad
모듬콩샐러드-콩.intro:
20231128, #breakfastdiary 906, -4°C/clear, 21min/workout(U) 
A couple of days ago I picked up a bag of mixed beans for a thousand won at Mangwon Market — you could tell the shopkeeper had a real eye for curation. Lately it's been the best value-for-happiness ingredient I've bought. 
Put the mixed beans in a pot and boil for about 20 minutes. (Green peas cook fast, so ideally you'd add them later, but I didn't have time to sort them out, so I just boiled everything together.)
Plate it up and add vinaigrette (3 olive oil, 1 wine vinegar, 0.5 whole grain mustard), lots of pepper, and mint, cilantro, or parsley if you have any. They're like the little star candies tucked into a pack of hardtack biscuits.

이슬아-고등어덮밥.title: Mackerel Rice Bowl
이슬아-고등어덮밥.intro:
20231127, #breakfastdiary 905, 5°C/drizzle
It's a world where stopping yourself feels as hard as dodging raindrops in the monsoon season. 스콘.title: Scones
스콘.intro:
20231022, #breakfastdiary 874, 3°C/sunny
I woke up early because of a dry cough. The sun was out, and I happened to have some clotted cream that needed using up, so why not make some warm bite-sized scones?
Recipe for 6 bite-sized scones:
Measure out 150g all-purpose flour, 30g sugar, 1t baking powder, and a pinch of salt, and mix together. Cut 30g butter into pieces and work it into the measured dry ingredients.
Add 50ml milk and 1 egg, mix well, then pour into the dry ingredients and knead into a dough. (Set aside a little of the milk-egg mixture.) Wrap it well and let it rest in the fridge for about 30 minutes.
Take out the dough, roll it out with a rolling pin, cut rounds with a mousse ring, place them on a tray, and brush with the reserved milk-egg mixture. Bake in a 170°C oven for about 15 minutes.
Cut in half and spread with jam, then cream.

The trouble is that language and writing live under the influence of complicated, delicate human relationships. Naming the subject of an action too clearly can seem rude, or land you in trouble for no good reason. Sometimes you simply don't know who the subject is. Sometimes the object is more familiar to the reader than the subject, or you want the focus to fall on whoever is affected. Saying 'the marine ecosystem was destroyed' can feel sadder than 'the Japanese government destroyed the marine ecosystem.'
(Kim Jin-hae, Embrace the Passive Voice)
Reading Lee O-deok's books, and having learned from a senior at the campus newspaper that sentences should always be written in the active voice as much as possible, I thought, well, there are sentences where the passive voice carries real force — and tried to write today's recipe in the passive voice. I failed.

마이야르-토스트-완두콩토스트.title: Maillard Toast with Peas

20230906 #breakfastdiary 838, 23°C/mostly clear, 21min/exercise(C)
Pour a little water into a pan, add green peas, and cook for 2-3 minutes. It's a low-moisture cooking method. Testing if they're done, I ate one — sweet, for frozen peas. Drain and set aside in a strainer.
Brush olive bread with olive oil and toast both sides until crisp, hoping for that #maillard reaction. Plate the toasted bread, then with the pan still warm, add a little olive oil and blanch the cooked peas. Thinking a touch of saltiness would be nice, I add some salt, and — technically it'd feel wrong to skip it — a bit of pepper to cut any off-flavor.
Pick up the bread and spread on ricotta cheese. Ricotta has good spreadability. (In terms of spreadability, cream cheese is the villain.) Pile the blanched peas generously on top and add parmesan cheese. Finish with a light dash of pepper — it'd feel wrong to skip that too.

This salmon can't decide whether it's about to spoil — so let's just grill it. Heat olive oil in a pan, sprinkle the salmon generously with pepper, and sear it crisp on all sides — front, back, top, bottom.
Mix 500ml of water with green tea powder that dissolves well even in cold water, and stir in about a spoonful of fish sauce. This condenses all the time and effort you'd normally spend on kelp, bonito flakes, and so on, into a curious flavor that's quick but not exactly deep.
Spoon rice into a bowl, sprinkle a little furikake, add the grilled salmon on top, and pour over the green tea.

감자-2.title: Potato Salad
감자-2.intro:
20230825, #breakfastdiary 827, 23°C/mostly cloudy
Boiled potatoes go dry and mealy after even half a day. Actually, 'dry and mealy' doesn't quite capture it - there should be a word for that specific letdown of a potato that's lost its flavor a while after being boiled. Like, the kind of word you'd mutter to yourself, half-joking, after pulling a potato out of the fridge - one you boiled, ate a piece or two of, and saved - and taking a bite. Something like, 'ugh, gone properly stale-potato on me.'
Anyway, so today's project is the so-called flavor-revival of this gone-stale potato. First, cut the potato into wedges, then blanch it in a pan with olive oil. Sauté. Roast. And season generously with salt, pepper, herbs, and above all, fresh rosemary, for the aroma. (sniff sniff) Ah, and don't forget the green olives - they're like the little star-shaped candies tucked inside a pack of gunbbang (Korean hardtack biscuits).
감자-2.ingredients: 2 potatoes, 1/2 cup green olives, 1T olive oil, 2t salt, 1t pepper, 1t mixed herbs, leaves from 1-2 sprigs of rosemary, a little parmesan cheese
감자-2.steps:
1. Cut the potatoes into wedges, skin on. 
2. Heat olive oil in a pan and roast the potatoes from step 1. Season with salt, pepper, mixed herbs, and rosemary leaves for flavor and aroma. 
3. Plate the potatoes from step 2, add the green olives, and grate parmesan cheese over the top.

한끼일기챌린지-깻잎과김자반을곁들인들기름카펠리니-들기름.title: Perilla Oil Capellini with Perilla Leaves and Gim-jaban
한끼일기챌린지-깻잎과김자반을곁들인들기름카펠리니-들기름.intro:
20230816, #breakfastdiary 819, 24°C/mostly clear
-
So, in the world according to Ms. Breakfast — a persona born on July 13, 2020 — a brand new breakfast must appear every single morning. Except, of course, on days when cooking breakfast simply isn't possible: the one morning a year of a health checkup (fasting required), or special occasions like business trips or travel. Otherwise, nearly every morning, a new breakfast has to show up. 
-
"Well, um, this is just my own personal ritual for starting the day. The one stretch of the day that's entirely mine to spend as I please, a way of chasing a little peace of mind, I guess?" Someone who once found out about my alter ego, Ms. Breakfast, asked how on earth I managed to cook something different every single morning, and that's how I answered. I privately rated my own response as pretty, quite, remarkably impressive-sounding. 
-
But honestly, that answer is, to some degree, both sincere and true. From the time the night before spent imagining and prepping the next morning's menu, to waking up and getting the ingredients ready and cooking, to recording the finished breakfast, and finally — the shortest part of all — actually eating it: every one of these moments is a fusion of sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch, elevated into something like a synesthetic experience. So wouldn't it be fair to call it a sacred ritual for starting the day? 
-
And so, the star of this long-winded #onemealdiarychallenge, today's one and only breakfast, is #perillaoilcapelliniwithperillaleavesandgimjaban. Capellini — nicknamed "angel hair" — deep-fried with seasoned salt and sugar to become a kind of "Korean furikake," combined with gim-jaban (seasoned seaweed flakes) and perilla leaves that somehow evoke oyakodon (the parent-and-child rice bowl), all tied together with perilla oil pressed from the very seeds of those leaves — doesn't that lineup rival Real Madrid's Galácticos era, with Zidane, Raúl, Beckham, and Figo all on the pitch together? If that sounds tempting, go check your kitchen right now for perilla leaves, gim-jaban, and capellini, and order some light-roasted perilla oil from @okhee_mill, the local mill reviving traditional oil culture!
1. Pour water into a pan, and once it boils, add a handful of capellini; when cooked, drain and rinse in cold water. 
2. Make a dressing with 2 parts Yondu, 2 parts water, and 1 part sugar. 
3. Plate the capellini, then add gim-jaban and chopped perilla leaves. (Adding ground perilla seed powder doubles the flavor explosion.) 
4. Elegantly drizzle over the dressing from step 2 and the perilla oil from Okhee Mill.

Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning 
Curious what "dead reckoning" actually meant, I looked it up: #deadreckoning is the practice of navigating using only the information you already have, once your signal has cut out. 
Take a car navigation system, for example — when a tunnel blocks the GPS signal and the algorithm keeps estimating your position anyway, that counts as dead reckoning too. These days, the gyro sensor in your smartphone supplies the data for it. 
It's never a good thing when everyday "dead reckoning" drags on too long. None of us are Ethan Hunt, after all.

1. Cut the peel off the orange with a knife and arrange the flesh on a plate. 
2. Tear mozzarella cheese by hand and arrange it nicely alongside. 
3. A little pepper, olive oil, and wine vinegar.

당근-관자-오렌지.title: Carrot, Scallop, and Orange Salad
당근-관자-오렌지.intro:
20230730, #breakfastdiary 802, 27°C/occasionally cloudy
A "spoiled at the last second" kind of breakfast — I finished the whole dish and then sprinkled ash (i.e., dried parsley flakes) all over it. Lesson learned: whenever possible, use fresh parsley, perilla leaves, or other herbs, finely chopped. 🥲
1. Julienne the carrots with a mandoline and salt them. Salt the scallops as well. 
2. Peel the orange into a bowl, add the drained carrots and scallops, then mix in olive oil, wine vinegar, 1 part lemon juice, and 1/2 part wholegrain mustard.

아보카도크로스티니.title: Avocado Crostini
아보카도크로스티니.intro:
20230729, #breakfastdiary 801, 28°C/mostly cloudy
Avocado crostini only works once the avocado is perfectly ripe — everything has its moment, so here's wishing everyone a good day, 
1. Toast bread brushed with olive oil in a hot pan. 
2. Squeeze the liquid from chopped tomato, then mix in 3 parts olive oil, 1 part wine vinegar, and 1/2 part wholegrain mustard. 
3. Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on the bread, then top with the tomato from step 2 and avocado. Cut half a lemon for its juice and zest.

푸님팟퐁커리.title: Crab-Stick Poo Pad Pong Curry
푸님팟퐁커리.intro:
20230728, #breakfastdiary 800, 26°C/mostly clear
"In the face of nature's vastness, everyday problems shrink down to size. More than anything, walking through nature is where we finally get to experience something close to a source, a wellspring. All five senses feel satisfied, and the heart feels full. Because we humans are, after all, part of nature."
(Albert Kitzler, the philosopher who writes about walking: "Learn Endurance by Walking," Longblack @longblack.co) 
For some people it's walking, for others it's drinks with friends, and for others still, it's breakfast — any of these can be that experience of touching something close to a source. 
(Since there's no actual crab🦀 in store-bought poo pad pong curry paste,) here's crab-stick poo pad pong curry — imitation crab meat coated in starch and fried crisp to mimic soft-shell crab. 
1. (Any brand works🙅) Tear the crab sticks into thick strips and coat evenly with starch. 
2. Heat oil in a pan and fry the starch-coated crab sticks until crisp. 
3. Add 100ml water and 1 beaten egg to store-bought crab poo pad pong curry sauce. 
4. Place the crab sticks from step 2 over rice and pour the curry from step 3 on top. Finish with green onion, 
#breakfast #recipe #miraclemorning here's #crabstickpoopadpongcurry

파스타-뇨끼.title: Gnocchi with Pesto and Peas
파스타-뇨끼.intro:
20230727, #breakfastdiary 799, 25°C/mostly cloudy
Greta Thunberg once said: "Water is pouring from a tap filling up a bathtub. If you refuse to turn off the tap, you are ignoring or denying the severity of the situation, and underestimating what will happen if you keep putting off the action needed to fix the problem right now."
(Source: SlowNews @slownewskr) 
And here we are, not even thinking about turning off the tap, just mopping up the water that's spilled onto the floor, 
1. Boil the gnocchi in water, then transfer to a bowl and toss with olive oil so it doesn't stick together. 
2. Heat olive oil in a pan, grate in some Parmesan, and sear the gnocchi until the surface turns crisp. 
3. Put the gnocchi in a bowl, add peas, mix in a good dollop of pesto. Finish with Parmesan and pepper, pepper,

밥-고등어오차즈케-오차즈케.title: Mackerel Ochazuke
밥-고등어오차즈케-오차즈케.intro:
20230726, #breakfastdiary 798, 25°C/mostly cloudy (the sun kept popping out and disappearing all morning) 
When I was little, my grandmother would sometimes soak my rice in chilled barley tea. This isn't quite as cool and refreshing as that was, but, 
1. Bring 500ml of water to a boil with a piece of kelp, then remove the kelp once it boils. 
2. Add bonito flakes to steep the broth, strain them out, then stir in 1 part tsuyu, 1 part mirim, and matcha. (A green tea bag works fine in place of matcha too👌) 
3. Pour the broth from step 2 over a bowl of rice, add a sprinkle of furikake, and top with grilled mackerel.

식물성스테이크-스테이크.title: Plant-Based Steak
식물성스테이크-스테이크.intro:
20230725 #breakfastdiary 797, 24°C/cloudy
1. Sear plant-based meat in a hot pan with a little oil.
2. Top with baby greens and tomato, drizzle with vinaigrette — the simplest #plantbasedsteak

알끈-아보카도-낫또.title: Avocado Natto Egg Bowl
알끈-아보카도-낫또.intro:
20230724 #breakfastdiary 796, 24°C/cloudy
There used to be a weird rumor that the chalaza (the little white string attached to the egg yolk) is loaded with cholesterol — but that's just a rumor. Most of the cholesterol in an egg is concentrated in the yolk, and the chalaza is really just protein.
1. Take out an avocado that's been ripening wrapped in newspaper, cut it in half, and slice it neatly.
2. Gently top a bowl of rice with avocado, natto, and egg yolk. (Since the rice isn't seasoned) I recommend pouring on about 2T of tsuyu and breaking the yolk to eat it bit by bit.

복숭아토스트.title: Peach Toast
복숭아토스트.intro:
20230723 #breakfastdiary 795, 25°C/heavy rain
I'm partial to the flashback scene near the end of La La Land.
1. Brush bread with olive oil and toast both sides in a hot pan.
2. Top with thinly sliced peach, prosciutto, honey, and fragrant mint.

복숭아-2.title: Peach Caprese Salad
복숭아-2.intro:
20230722 #breakfastdiary 794, 28°C/mostly cloudy
"Because we don't know when we'll die, we end up thinking of life as a spring that never runs dry. But nothing in this world happens an infinite number of times — the reality is that everything happens only a vanishingly small number of times. (...) How many more times will I get to see a full moon? Maybe twenty. And yet, even so, we go on thinking as if the number were infinite."
(Ryuichi Sakamoto: The Musician Who Longed for Nature, Playing Eternity Through Subtraction, @longblack.co)
…
1. Wash the peaches well, cut into wedges, and arrange with basil and mozzarella.
2. Drizzle evenly with a mix of olive oil and wine vinegar, then finish with honey for a touch of sweetness.

푸실리파스타-푸실리-파스타.title: Fusilli Pasta
푸실리파스타-푸실리-파스타.intro:
20230721 #breakfastdiary 793, 24°C/occasionally cloudy
Like the way the internet has drifted from book-like early web pages and blogs toward listicles, videos, and short-form clips, it looks as though people are increasingly drawn to shorter stories — but really, humans have always preferred short, simple stories, and those are the ones that tend to do relatively well.
So here's today's breakfast: a truly short and simple #fusillipasta recipe — fingers crossed it does well too 🙏🏻
1. Boil fusilli in salted water for about 10 minutes. (Since there's no other seasoning, the amount of salt here decides the flavor.)
2. In a bowl, add basil, tomato, camembert cheese, and half a clove of minced garlic.
3. Pour in the cooked fusilli along with some pasta water. Add plenty of pepper, mix well, and enjoy.

햇감자-포카칩.title: New Potato Chips with Tzatziki
햇감자-포카칩.intro:
20230720 #breakfastdiary 792, 24°C/mostly cloudy
Potatoes are one of Korea's four major staple crops, harvested four times a year. Greenhouse spring potatoes come in March–May, field-grown spring potatoes in June–July, and highland potatoes from August to November. Fall potatoes hit the market from October through the following January. Field-grown spring potatoes and highland potatoes together make up 70% of the year's total production, so when supply is highest, prices are lowest — and the flavor is at its best too.
(Even potato chips have a season? Why chips taste better in June)
It's easy to miss, but the bags of Poca Chips sold around this time of year are labeled "100% Korean new potatoes." (The rest of the year, they use regular potatoes instead.) It's a seasonal food you can only really taste around now.
1. Open a bag of Poca Chips made from seasonal new potatoes.
2. Dip them in the tzatziki I made a few days ago.

옥수수쏨땀-카리스마.title: Corn Som Tam
옥수수쏨땀-카리스마.intro:
20230719 #breakfastdiary 791, 24°C/mostly clear, 21min/workout(C)
"Because charisma is understood only as a way of behaving, politicians stage it and act as though they have it. Citizens of modern democracies reject or grow suspicious of charismatic leadership — yet they're still often fooled by, and even get swept up in, 'fake charisma.'"
(Kim Yong-seop, Charisma: What Matters Isn't Style but the Substance of the Task)
If the conviction, will, and drive that come to mind when you hear the word 'charisma' are just means to an end rather than the substance itself, then couldn't there be such a thing as a charismatic corn som tam?
1. Mix 1/2T minced garlic, 1T fish sauce, and 1T lime juice to make the dressing. (Skipping the chili since it's breakfast.)
2. Cut tomato into bite-size pieces and pour over the dressing from step 1.
3. Add blanched green beans, julienned carrot, and corn, and toss together. Instead of peanuts, add some fried shallots for crunch.

치즈프로슈토꿀토스트-프로슈토.title: Cheese Prosciutto Honey Toast
치즈프로슈토꿀토스트-프로슈토.intro:
20230718 #breakfastdiary 790, 23°C/drizzle, 21min/workout(Y)
Honey and prosciutto make a perfect sweet-and-salty combo.
1. Brush bread with olive oil and toast in a hot pan.
2. Plate the toast and top with camembert cheese, prosciutto, honey, and basil.
Super simple #cheeseprosciuttohoneytoast

차지키소스를곁들인호밀크래커-차지키.title: Rye Crackers with Tzatziki
차지키소스를곁들인호밀크래커-차지키.intro:
20230717 #breakfastdiary 789, 23°C/cloudy
It's raining, and even as it rains,
one who is already wet does not get wet again.
(Oh Kyu-won, Even in the Rain, One Who Is Wet)
1. Julienne 1 cucumber, sprinkle with salt, let sit briefly, then squeeze firmly to remove the moisture.
2. Mix the drained cucumber with 5T Greek yogurt and 5 cloves of minced garlic.
3. (No dill on hand, so) add 1T herbs, 1T olive oil, 1T lemon juice, plenty of salt and pepper to make the tzatziki sauce.
4. Spoon the tzatziki onto rye crackers, and (since it looked a little bare) finish with pink peppercorns.

토마토-바질.title: Tomato Basil Toast
토마토-바질.intro:
20230716 #breakfastdiary 788, 24°C/drizzle
Peace of mind is a luxury — sometimes even an ordinary steady mind feels out of reach. Chopping tomatoes and basil, I find myself thinking about staying even-keeled.
1. Put bread in a hot pan, brush with olive oil, and toast both sides.
2. Chop 3 tomatoes and a good amount of basil, mix in 3T mayonnaise. (It's best to scoop out the tomato seeds first.)
3. Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on the toast and top with the mixture from step 2. Add a little extra salt to taste if you like.

펜네페스토파스타-펜네-파스타.title: Penne Pesto Pasta
펜네페스토파스타-펜네-파스타.intro:
20230715 #breakfastdiary 787, 22°C/cloudy
Boil noodles, drain, and toss with sauce — as simple as instant jjajangmyeon or bibim noodles: #pennepestopasta
1. Boil penne in well-salted water.
2. Once cooked, drain into a bowl and drizzle with olive oil so it doesn't stick. Add pesto and mix evenly.
3. Add roughly chopped basil and a few green olives.

샥슈카.title: Shakshuka
샥슈카.intro:
20230714 #breakfastdiary 786, 24°C/rain (seriously, it's rained all week),
The simplest shakshuka in the world
1. In a clay pot, bring 5T store-bought tomato sauce and 2T water to a boil.
2. Crack in two eggs, add mozzarella cheese, and cover with a lid for a bit.
3. Top with chopped basil. Eat once the egg whites are just set.

토마토달걀볶음-토달볶-토마토.title: Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
토마토달걀볶음-토달볶-토마토.intro:
20230713 #breakfastdiary 785, 24°C/drizzle, 21min/workout(L)
Written as #tomatoeggstirfry, read as #tomatoscramble.
1. Sauté oil and scallion in a pan. Right about the moment you think, 'uh oh, is this burning?' — add the tomato.
2. Beat 3 eggs with 5T milk and a pinch of salt, and set aside.
3. Push the tomato to one side of the pan, pour in the egg mixture, and stir-fry. Once the egg is just about set, mix it together with the tomato.
*For a better egg texture, I'd recommend scrambling the egg first, setting it aside, then stir-frying the tomato and adding the egg back in afterward.

베이글맛집-타르데마-베이글.title: Tardemah Bagel
베이글맛집-타르데마-베이글.intro:
20230712 #breakfastdiary 784, 23°C/cloudy
This is 🥯 the #bagelspot, Tardemah @tardemah_

1. Slice an Earl Grey bagel horizontally and toast in a pan.
2. Spread one half with three kinds of cream cheese — sun-dried tomato basil, cheongyang chili bacon, and honey cinnamon — plus kaya salted butter.

레몬파스타-레몬-파스타.title: Lemon Pasta
레몬파스타-레몬-파스타.intro:
20230711 #breakfastdiary 783, 24°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(U)
A refreshing #lemonpasta that says summer has arrived
1. Boil capellini in salted water. (This is the first and only seasoning, so make it good and salty.)
2. Sauté butter and minced garlic in a pan. (Sliced garlic would be even better, but I didn't have any.)
3. Add the capellini to the pan with a ladle of pasta water and a knob of butter. Time to mantecare.
4. Plate it up with an egg yolk, parmesan cheese, and half a lemon — zested and squeezed for juice.

토마토-4.title: Tomato Parsley Salad
토마토-4.intro:
20230710 #breakfastdiary 782, 22°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
Making breakfast every day means I always need a little leafy green on hand, and parsley, perilla leaves, and (among mints) spearmint keep especially well compared to other greens — they're incredibly handy.
With rain forecast all week, I feel like I need to brace both body and mind.
1. Wash the large and small tomatoes.
2. Slice the large tomato and lay it on the plate as a base; cut the small tomatoes into sixths (quartering made them a bit too big) and scatter on top. Sprinkle with chopped parsley.
3. Drizzle evenly with vinaigrette.
#breakfast #recipe #miraclemorning #tomato, parsley

감자-3.title: Baked Potato with Cheddar and Bacon
감자-3.intro:
20230709 #breakfastdiary 781, 24°C/cloudy
1. Wash the potatoes well, score them lengthwise with vertical cuts, and let them sit in water for a bit.
2. Brush the potatoes with melted butter and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
3. Chop bacon finely and pan-fry it; mince the parsley.
4. Take the potatoes out of the oven, cut cheddar cheese into quarters, and tuck the pieces into the slits. Bake at 180°C for about 10 minutes, until the cheese melts.
5. Plate the potatoes and top with Greek yogurt and the bacon and parsley from step 3.

대파그라땅-크림수프-대파.title: Leek Gratin in Cream Sauce
대파그라땅-크림수프-대파.intro:
20230708 #breakfastdiary 780, 25°C/cloudy
1. Mix 2T cream soup, 2T milk, 1/2T grated garlic, 2T parmesan cheese, 1/2T wholegrain mustard, and herbs to make the sauce. (Adjust the thickness by adding more milk.)
2. Cut the leeks, arrange them neatly, pour the sauce over, and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.
3. Take it out of the oven, sprinkle with parmesan cheese, and bake again at 200°C for 20 minutes.
1. For the roux: melt butter in a pan and stir in flour in two additions, using a 1:1 butter-to-flour ratio.
2. The roux-to-milk ratio is 1:7 — pour the milk into the roux and stir to loosen it. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

가지-그릭요거트.title: Grilled Eggplant with Greek Yogurt
가지-그릭요거트.intro:
20230707 #breakfastdiary 797, 23°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
You should have seen the vivid purple that flashes for just a moment when eggplant is cooked through, right before it turns reddish-brown.
1. Wash the eggplant well, halve it, and cook in a hot pan with olive oil. It softens quickly, so start with the cut side down.
2. Mix half a shallot, 3T olive oil, 1T wine vinegar, and 1/2T wholegrain mustard to make the dressing.
3. Plate the eggplant, spoon over the dressing, and finish with Greek yogurt, red pepper flakes, and parsley.

당근-3.title: Roasted Carrots with Parmesan
당근-3.intro:
20230706 #breakfastdiary 796, 24°C/mostly clear
The smell of parmesan cheese (grated) roasting in the oven is pretty irresistible.
1. Wash the carrots, peel them, and cut into bite-size pieces.
2. Make a sauce with olive oil, minced parsley, salt, pepper, paprika powder, and red pepper flakes.
3. Toss the carrots in the sauce, roll them in parmesan cheese, and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes.

만두-2.title: Cold Dumplings with Vinegar-Soy Dressing
만두-2.intro:
20230705 #breakfastdiary 795, 21°C/cloudy
"I've never once told anyone I 'failed.' It was simply a mistake. These days, young people use that frightening word — 'failure' — far too often. When we resist the word 'failure,' we become able to enjoy our mistakes and our pain."
(Kim Chang-il, terminal business owner, one of the world's top 100 collectors, on the artist C-Kim's dream)
Failure isn't something to fear (doesn't Finland even have a Day for Failure?), but it doesn't need to be a constant refrain either.
1. Blanch store-bought water dumplings in boiling water, then plate them.
2. Mix 3T water, 1T soy sauce, 1T vinegar, 1T sugar, and a splash of sesame oil for the dressing, and pour over the dumplings. Finish with chopped scallion.

라따뚜이.title: Ratatouille
라따뚜이.intro:
20230704 #breakfastdiary 794, 25°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
In Korean it's 'ratatouille,' but read the way the French actually pronounce it, it's more like 'ha-ta-too-ee.'
1. Wash the eggplant, zucchini, and tomato well, and slice them into rounds.
2. Pour tomato sauce into an oven-safe pot, then layer in the eggplant, zucchini, and tomato.
3. Drizzle with olive oil, add plenty of salt and pepper, and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes — it came out a little underdone, so 30 minutes would probably be better.
Forgot the parmesan cheese, but anyway, a simple #ratatouille for a busy morning.

복숭아샐러드-복숭아-조니그린우드.title: Peach Ricotta Salad
복숭아샐러드-복숭아-조니그린우드.intro:
20230703 #breakfastdiary 793, 24°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/workout(C)
Starting the second half of 2023 with a #peachsalad
1. Rinse the peaches well under running water, cut into sixths, and arrange on a plate.
2. Add ricotta cheese and almonds, then finish with olive oil and (today, an extra-tangy) wine vinegar dressing.
Also, currently on a #jonnygreenwood binge

가지-가지덮밥.title: Braised Eggplant Rice Bowl
가지-가지덮밥.intro:
20230702 #breakfastdiary 792, 25°C/cloudy
1. Wash the eggplant, peel it, and steam it.
2. Make a sauce with 1T oyster sauce, 3T soy sauce, and 1T honey.
3. Put the steamed eggplant in a pan, pour over the sauce, and simmer down.
4. Top a bowl of rice with the eggplant, an egg yolk, chopped scallion, sesame seeds, and sesame oil.
A soft, moist eggplant rice bowl even my mother, who has trouble chewing, can enjoy.

또띠아-피자.title: Tortilla Pizza
또띠아-피자.intro:
20230701 #breakfastdiary 791, 25°C/mostly clear
1. Lay a tortilla in a pan, add mozzarella cheese, and cover with a lid until the cheese melts.
2. While the cheese melts, mix 3T mayonnaise, 2T honey, 1T lemon juice, and plenty of pepper to make a dressing.
3. Plate the tortilla and drizzle on the dressing.
4. Top with well-washed spinach and sautéed ham (bacon would probably suit it even better). Finish with parmesan cheese.
A keystone that serves no structural purpose was carved as decoration above a square window, and people happily paid a higher price for a house whose ornamentation gave off an air of old-world elegance. Form and function had drifted apart, but that gap was smoothed over by the familiarity we call taste.
(Lim Woo-jin, The Origin of Ornament)
The keystone, which once bore the weight at the center of an arch, has somewhere along the way lost its original function and kept only its form. How many things around us are just like that?

시금치토마토치즈랩-토마토-시금치.title: Spinach Tomato Cheese Wrap
시금치토마토치즈랩-토마토-시금치.intro:
20230630 #breakfastdiary 790, 22°C/cloudy, 20min/workout(Y)
Are you doing okay —
even though we meet every day,
that's still what I most want to know.
'Yeah,' I answer with a nod,
and even that is the heaviest single syllable.
(Kim So-yeon, No Return 5)
1. Melt a knob of butter in a pan and blanch the spinach.
2. Add tomato, cheese, and two beaten eggs, then gently cover with a tortilla and flip after 1–2 minutes.
3. After another 1–2 minutes, take the tortilla out of the pan, let it cool slightly, roll it up like a gimbap, and cut it in half.
I'll call this one a #spinachtomatocheesewrap — plump, since I packed in so many fillings.

아보카도수란토스트-아보카도-수란.title: Avocado Poached Egg Toast
아보카도수란토스트-아보카도-수란.intro:
20230629 #breakfastdiary 789, 23°C/rain, 30min/workout(Y)
Monsoon season has begun.
1. Brush bread with olive oil and toast both sides in a hot pan.
2. Top with mayonnaise, half an avocado, and a poached egg, then finish with red pepper flakes. #avocadopoachedeggtoast

순두부계란찜-순두부-계란.title: Soft Tofu Steamed Egg
순두부계란찜-순두부-계란.intro:
20230628 #breakfastdiary 788, 22°C/cloudy
1. Beat two eggs in a bowl, add 150ml water and a little chicken stock to season.
2. Cut in half a block of soft tofu and some scallion, microwave for 3 minutes, and finish with a swirl or two of sesame oil.
A simple 3-minute #softtofusteamedegg for a busy morning.
—
Don't cry
surely you have somewhere to return to
even you
how could you have nowhere to return to
groping along a wall
riddled with holes
crying in secret, you
sobbing like a palm tree caught by the hair
you, hiding on an island
you, drifting off the island
don't cry
you, forever heading west no matter how far you go
even you
how could you have nowhere to return to
(Lee Hong-seop, You, Forever Heading West)

20230620-조식다이어리-788-21도-후림-21분-운동-C.title: Peas, Broccoli & Tempeh with Sunny-Side-Up Egg
20230620-조식다이어리-788-21도-후림-21분-운동-C.intro:
20230620 #breakfastdiary 788, 21°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(C)
Low-moisture boiled peas and broccoli with olive oil, salt, and pepper, blanched mushrooms and tempeh, cherry tomatoes, and a sunny-side-up egg

당근샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드-당근.title: Carrot Salad
당근샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드-당근.intro:
20230619 #breakfastdiary 787, 25°C/mostly clear, 21min/workout(Y)
Boiled carrots are a real love-it-or-hate-it thing. What do boiled carrots mean to you?
1. Wash the carrots, peel them, and boil for about 10 minutes.
2. Drain and place in a bowl, then mix in butter, salt, pepper, and parsley.
3. Plate it up with one more knob of butter on top. #carrotsalad
This is my #mylocalfoodsalad recipe.
Looks like rice cake tteokbokki, but it's actually carrot salad.

라임-라임우동-누벨바그.title: Lime Udon
라임-라임우동-누벨바그.intro:
20230608 #breakfastdiary 777, 18°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
Lime udon — something I make once summer rolls around, and each year the taste gets a little better (proud of that).
The real charm of lime is that bittersweet finish, a flavor only grown-ups who've been through the wringer really understand.
(Broth)
1. Bring 1 liter of water to a boil with 2 sheets of dried kelp and 2 dried shiitake mushrooms. Once boiling, remove the kelp, add bonito flakes, and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes. Strain to prepare the broth.
2. Mix in 2 parts tsuyu, 2 parts mirin, and 1 part sugar. (Seasoning is kept light rather than strong.)
*Making the broth ahead of time means an easy meal even on a busy morning. (5-minute cut)
(Noodles)
1. Boil store-bought udon noodles for 2 minutes, then rinse in cold water (ice would be nice, but this works too) for extra chewy texture.
2. Place the noodles in a bowl, pour over the broth, and top with sliced lime.

유니버설디자인-배리어프리-토마토부라타치즈샐러드.title: Tomato Burrata Salad
유니버설디자인-배리어프리-토마토부라타치즈샐러드.intro:
20230530 #breakfastdiary 775, 19°C/mostly cloudy
A few months ago at the city art museum, here and there I noticed two versions of the wall text for certain works — and under the shorter, simpler version was this note:
This description was written in easy-to-understand language.
Exhibit descriptions have always felt needlessly dense to me, so I was genuinely glad to see this effort, and I recently found out where it came from. Why should #UniversalDesign and #BarrierFree be limited to physical constraints? I'm adding some content from the website of Soso Communication (@sosocommunication), a company that provides easy-to-understand information.
Soso Communication provides easy information for everyone.
'Easy information' is essential for people with developmental disabilities, foreign residents, children with learning disabilities, and older adults — anyone who finds words and text hard to follow — but really, it makes life easier for all of us. Soso Communication is here for a life free of communication barriers, down to the small, everyday moments.
Today's breakfast is cherry tomatoes, burrata, and mint with a vinaigrette — a #TomatoBurrataSalad that's exactly as simple and honest as it looks.

살구토스트-살구.title: Apricot Toast
살구토스트-살구.intro:
20230529 #breakfastdiary 774, 24°C/rain, 21min/workout(Y)
Poaching apricots with sugar gave them the prettiest color I've ever seen.
1. Wash the apricots well, cut into quarters, then poach over medium heat with sugar and the juice of half a lemon. (Use sugar at about 1/5 the weight of the apricots, though you can adjust to taste.) Once done, chill in the fridge.
2. Sear bread in a hot pan with olive oil, then top with burrata and dill.
3. Spoon the apricot compote from step 1 on top and finish with mint.

계란찜-푸딩같은계란찜.title: Almost-Pudding Steamed Egg
계란찜-푸딩같은계란찜.intro:
20230528 #breakfastdiary 773, 19°C/rain, 21min/workout(U)
The recipe promised this would turn out just like a pudding-like steamed egg, but the edges ended up as plain old steamed egg. Following a recipe to the letter doesn't guarantee the same result. There's no single right answer in breakfast — or in life.
1. Beat 4 eggs well, add a pinch of salt and 200ml water, mix, then strain through a sieve.
2. Pour into a bowl, skim off the foam, steam over low heat for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for about 5 minutes.
3. Make a sauce with 1 part oyster sauce, 1 part oligosaccharide syrup, and 1/2 part each of soy sauce and sesame oil, then pour it over the steamed egg.

꼰낄리에샐러드-꼰낄리에.title: Conchiglie Pasta Salad

20230527 #breakfastdiary 772, 20°C/cloudy
Rain hurrying summer along, and a seafood metaphor to match — #ConchiglieSalad.
1. Boil the conchiglie pasta in salted water.
2. Sear shiitake mushrooms in a hot pan with olive oil, then use the remaining heat to cook the zucchini.
3. Blanch the peas with minimal water, then add a bit more water and blanch the mussels.
4. Combine 1 through 3 in a bowl and dress with a vinaigrette. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

완두콩수란샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드-수란.title: Poached Egg and Pea Salad
완두콩수란샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드-수란.intro:

Even frozen peas, blanched with just a little water, bring out a lovely, subtle sweetness.
1. Once the water boils, turn off the heat, add 1 part vinegar, wait a moment, then gently slip in the egg to poach it quietly.
2. Blanch the peas with minimal water, plate them together with the poached egg, and top with a vinaigrette. Finish with parmesan. #PeaAndPoachedEggSalad
This is a recipe from #MyLocalFoodSalad.

참외-참외샐러드.title: Korean Melon Salad

'Its flowers bloom fine, and its fruit is bountiful' —
a line from Canto 2 of the Yongbieocheonga (Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven); this really is the season when flowers are lovely and fruit grows abundant.
1. Wash one Korean melon well and peel it with a julienne peeler (the kind used for som tam).
2. Cut it in half, scoop out the seeds, strain the juice, and mix in white balsamic, salt, and pepper to make a dressing.
3. Slice the halved melon neatly, arrange on a plate, and spoon over the dressing from step 2.

광화문글판-토스트.title: Lemon Parsley Burrata Toast

Today's breakfast is a very summery lemon parsley burrata toast.
1. Brush a pan with olive oil and toast the bread until hot.
2. Spread burrata on the bread, spoon over the dressing, and finish with mint.
*Dressing: 6 parts olive oil, 1 part herbs, 6 parts lemon juice, a little minced garlic, chopped parsley, salt, pepper, and lemon zest to taste.
(In place of chopped parsley, I'd recommend basil or perilla leaves, sliced into long strips rather than chopped.)

소만-살구샐러드-나의로컬푸드샐러드.title: Grilled Apricot Salad

2. Plate the seared apricots, then top with burrata and mint.

파스타-토마토마리네이드.title: Marinated Tomato Pasta
파스타-토마토마리네이드.intro:
20230521 #breakfastdiary 766, 19°C/partly cloudy, 26min/workout(U)
Capellini works beautifully in a cold pasta. A verb turned noun — marinated tomato pasta.
(Marinated tomatoes)
1. Score the cherry tomatoes, blanch in hot water, then transfer to cold water and peel.
2. Mince half an onion, then toss with the cherry tomatoes, 30ml olive oil, balsamic (oh wait, none left — add more honey instead), honey, 10ml lemon juice each, and a little salt. (Add basil or another herb if you have it.) Chill in the fridge to serve cold.

1. Boil the capellini in salted water.
2. Rinse the noodles in cold water, transfer to a bowl, and toss with olive oil.
3. Plate the noodles and top with the marinated tomatoes. Parmesan on top is a nice touch too.

A flour-free, low-carb pizza absolutely loaded with vegetables.
1. Prep zucchini, button mushrooms, bell pepper, and broccoli, arrange on a pan, drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast in a 200°C oven for 20 minutes.
2. Mix tomato sauce and parmesan with garlic powder and herbs, then spread evenly over the vegetables.
3. Top with red onion, cherry tomatoes, and mozzarella, drizzle with olive oil, and bake for another 10 minutes at 200°C.

"In painting, there are those who know it, those who love it, those who merely look at it, and those who collect it. If all you do is hoard paintings, you can't be said to really look at them; and if you look but only make out the paint on the surface, you can't yet be said to love them. Even if you love them, if all you're after is color and form, you can't yet be said to know them. To know a painting means to grasp not only its technique but the subtle principle and spirit that don't readily meet the eye. So the true pleasure of painting lies in truly knowing it — once you know it, you come to truly love it; once you love it, you come to truly see it; once you can truly see, you come to collect; and what you collect then is something altogether different from mere hoarding."
This appears in the preface Professor Yu Hong-june wrote for #mytreasuredheritage — the source of the line "Once you know, you see; once you see, you come to love; and what you see then is no longer what it once was" is a piece by Yu Han-jun, a writer of King Jeongjo's era.

When you sear a steak in plenty of oil over high heat, almost frying it, the outside turns crisp and the Maillard reaction kicks in — that process is called #searing. Easier said than done, though: most of the time the outside burns before the inside is cooked. I don't really go for meat, so I rarely cook it, and while I was wondering how to handle this expensive, unfamiliar ingredient, I came across #reversesearing.
It's a method that uses the oven instead of a sous vide machine (though the idea is similar) — cooking the meat evenly at a low temperature over a long time, then finishing with a quick sear. Supposedly it has a fairly low failure rate.
-Let the tenderloin come to room temperature, then cook it in a 90°C oven for 40 minutes. (The tenderloin was marinated beforehand with salt and pepper.)
-Pour oil in a pan and flip it twice, 30 seconds each side; then add butter and rosemary and baste while flipping twice more, 30 seconds each side.
That was the plan, but the moment the meat actually started cooking in front of me, oil spattering everywhere, my breathing sped up, my hands got clumsy, and all those neat numbers — 30 seconds, twice — went out the window. Watching the video I took afterward, I'd clearly seared it quite a bit more than planned, so my intended medium-well went out the window too, leaving just well-done.
Once again: in the moment you're actually facing a task, what decides success or failure isn't a meticulous plan so much as practiced hands. In the end, there's no substitute for doing it many times.
As for steak, since I'm not that big on meat, I doubt I'll ever get around to cooking it skillfully.

#GokCha (literally 'grain tea') is a monk's euphemism for alcohol. The story goes that a Joseon-era monk, Great Master Jinmuk, felt a bit sheepish about drinking and started calling it 'tea' (cha) instead — and that's supposedly where the term comes from.
Songhwa Baegiljju, passed down for nearly 400 years by the head monk of Suwangsa Temple in Jeollabuk-do, is probably the best-known example of this kind of 'grain tea.' Alcohol was forbidden in temples, but it also served as a means of practice. I like to think that's not so different from enjoying a quiet drink alone now and then, just to listen to your inner voice.
A crepe eaten alongside #sikhye (sweet rice drink), which has a bit of that 'grain tea' feeling —

This morning, half-asleep with my eyes barely open, I read something that really struck me.
Still, the reason our lives are better than a movie is that they have a warmth we can actually hold.
There are moments when I think to myself, 'wow, that just felt like a movie.' Like during an exam, when time is racing by second by second and my hands, moving in a hurry, feel strangely satisfying. Or in the late-afternoon hallway after school, when the sunlight stretches long across the floor and the only sound is a single set of footsteps. Some days it rains and yet my heart feels oddly dry and warm, or someone touches my hair without warning and the back of my neck tingles. Ah, just a little more — I wish it had lasted a little longer. Or that I could come back to that exact moment whenever I wanted. I kept looking into some living room from some particular day, glittering through gaps in green leaves, until the sun sank all the way into the sunset.
So how wonderful would it be if only these moments were like a movie.
But the moments that feel like a movie without my wanting them to are the long, endless mock exam when I buried my face in the test paper and cried in secret. The times I ended up getting angry at moments I shouldn't have. The times I was swept up in feelings no one could understand, because no one was patiently watching me the way an audience watches a character. It's strange — in dramas, it's fine to cry and wail like that. The characters just pour everything out, become as miserable as they possibly can, and then, cut — that's it. But it was only by actually living through it that I learned that's not how it works for me. No matter how sad I was, I still had a duty to keep going to whatever came next. I have no choice, even if I don't want to. Because there's no one to call 'cut' for us.
Unlike the villain, for whom everything felt meaningless, nothing felt meaningless to me — and that was exactly what made it so painful. Everything mattered too much, so in the end I wanted to pile it all onto the same bagel anyway. Dividing things into take A and take B, unable to cut out a single scene of my own life in order to create the most efficient possible emotional payoff within a limited time. So how precious is this inefficiency we're allowed. Since I'm the only one watching everything anyway, I don't have to worry about any other audience. If I want, I can stretch out and replay a scene I love for as long as I like, endlessly. If I don't like something, I can change the genre halfway through on a whim, cry and laugh like in a movie, and clean up the mess afterward without it looking graceful at all. That is exactly the freedom we have outside the movies. A human warmth you could never feel on the other side of the screen is born in this very moment. Most of it will be scenes that are cut, skipped, left unpolished — messy but diligently cleaned up, one way or another.

Since the 1950s, foreign language proficiency has been evaluated across speaking, listening, reading, and writing, on a scale running from 'unable to use the language' (level 0) to 'equivalent to an educated native speaker' (level 5). Most diplomats aimed for 'professional working proficiency' (level 3), while those generally considered 'fluent in a foreign language' were rated level 4, and those at a 'near-native level' were rated 4+.
But an interesting shift appears in the new standard adopted in 2022. Level 5 ('equivalent to an educated native speaker') and level 4+ ('near-native level') were merged into a single 'level 4,' dropping the term 'native speaker' altogether in favor of 'advanced proficiency.' In other words, the goal of achieving 'native-like' skill was removed from foreign language learning altogether. This reflects a shift, since the 2000s, in how foreign language education has come to view the whole idea of the 'native speaker.'
(Robert Fouser, 'As the Age of Native-Speakerism Comes to a Close')
This change in the evaluation standards of the Foreign Service Institute, which teaches foreign languages to American diplomats, hints at a broader shift of the times. What matters now isn't sounding like a native speaker so much as 'the ability to understand and adapt across different cultures.'

They had a lot of stuff, so I helped carry it, and they said, 'Let's grab coffee sometime.' I couldn't quite bring myself to say it back — it felt too ordinary a thing to say. And that's when I realized we weren't the kind of people who'd actually reach out and meet up separately. But I didn't think the remark was insincere. I think it was the best thing that person could offer in that moment. 
It's a cliché, but when you think of it as the best warmth a person can show in that situation, it becomes touching. Even an everyday phrase like that stays with someone's face in your memory — so when I think that the words I say today could become the last words I leave with someone, I find myself not wanting to let a single word go to waste.

In Korean, the verb doesn't come right after the subject — it comes at the very end of the sentence. So when a sentence gets long, the gap between subject and verb widens, and it becomes confusing to tell what's being said about what. That's why, to make Korean easier to follow, you need to insert a verb partway through that clarifies the subject — deliberately narrowing that gap. Which is why it's better to write Korean in short sentences.
Yoon Yeo-kyung, Why Should You Write in 'Short Sentences'? Because of How Korean Is Structured

"I realized I couldn't chase down and get involved in every single decision along the way. So I trust them. I believe that person is doing their best in their own way, and I'm doing my best in mine.
When a designer trusts and hands things over to an engineer, I learned that the engineer actually works even harder to realize the designer's intent. Service is supposed to keep improving, but it produces a paradox of its own. Consumers who keep experiencing great service raise their expectations higher and higher, making it harder for companies to satisfy them. It's a bit like how, once you've eaten something delicious enough times, at some point it stops tasting so delicious — or how the more special treatment you get, the more you forget to be grateful for it.
For instance, when American Airlines first introduced its mileage program, every customer was thrilled and thankful. Now, the smallest inconvenience with using those miles draws furious complaints. Today's consumer market is caught in what's called the 'hedonic treadmill' or 'satisfaction treadmill' — the more happiness you feel, the higher the bar rises, until you can no longer feel happy at all.
Maybe that's the same psychology behind customers cheering for the foul-mouthed grandmother at #YokjaengiHalmoni and craving her #SsangyokLatte (the 'double-cursing latte').

At Belgian and German train stations, announcements are mostly about departure times and locations, delays, or platform changes. On subways and buses, they announce destinations, and in Germany, where masks are mandatory, mask announcements come in both German and English. That's about it.
Korea is different. Every time a subway car's doors open and close, there's an announcement telling you they're opening, they're closing, be careful. Since COVID-19, every bus ride comes with a mask reminder — not just when you board, but every time anyone else boards too.
In other words, what Germany and Belgium reserve for truly necessary announcements, Korea treats as a kind of customer-care service. At first glance, Korea looks more customer-centered. But think again, and it seems more about the service provider showing off their diligence through that so-called consideration than about the customer at all.
Robert Fouser, Announcements: Between Consideration and Control

Researchers at UC Riverside recently announced in the June issue of the journal Nature Food that they succeeded in developing a highly energy-efficient food production system by linking artificial photosynthesis with living organisms.
The researchers developed a highly efficient catalyst that uses light, water, and carbon dioxide to produce acetate through artificial photosynthesis. Acetate, made of just two carbon atoms, functions almost like a cure-all in living organisms.
They fed this lab-made acetate to a range of organisms — algae, yeast, mushrooms, lettuce, rice, rapeseed, and tomatoes. These organisms not only used the absorbed acetate as an energy source but also converted it into amino acids, sugars, and other biomolecules to grow and multiply. As a result, they thrived even without any light at all.

The first keyword has to be <Daily Isula>. Starting a mailing subscription service with the catchy pitch 'one piece a day, ten thousand won a month, five hundred won a piece,' <Daily Isula> created a new model of direct trade between reader and writer.
Second, the 'Korea Science Fiction Literary Award.' Kim Cho-yeop, author of <If We Can't Go at the Speed of Light>, and Cheon Seon-ran, author of <A Thousand Blues>, are among its winners.

Naturally, <My Liberation Notes> doesn't move toward a familiar redemption narrative either. Its characters aren't saved. They're only changed, ever so slightly, by someone who comes from a completely different world. The show is full of small, everyday enemies that torment its characters. Unlike a typical Korean drama, they aren't punished on moral grounds. They don't repent, either. They'll probably go on living as the same flawed people even after the show ends. The Yeom family and Mr. Gu don't get the ending we expected, either. Someone dies suddenly. Someone suddenly meets a new person. Someone starts dreaming of a job they never once considered. And with that, the drama ends abruptly, as if to say there's no such thing as a perfect happy ending in our lives — that life is less like the ten-lane Gangnam-daero and more like an unpredictable country road in some rural town, full of the bloated corpses of frogs that never made it across. The brand name #IKEA is pronounced "eye-KEE-ah" almost exclusively in English-speaking countries, rather than "ee-KAY-ah." Many believe it comes from the word "idea," but it actually comes from the founder's name and hometown.
Meanwhile, IKEA's product naming follows these rules:
Lamps = words from chemistry, music, and meteorology
Curtains = women's names
Desks, chairs, shelves = men's names
Bookcases, sofas, coffee tables = Swedish place names
Bathroom products = Scandinavian rivers, lakes, and bays

A man hands over a boiled egg.
According to the weather forecast, around one o'clock
the train will run into sleet near Daejeon.
Because the heating system is a mess,
a few masked passengers cough out
coughs like damp cigarette filters,
and into consciousness too damp to fall easily asleep,
the dim cabin lights keep flickering off for moments.

Do you understand the feeling of leaving Seoul for good?
You must be heading back to your hometown.
This time, really, I'm retiring to the countryside for good.
As if he'd hurt his fingertip peeling the eggshell,
the man falls silent for a moment.
I finished high school in Jochiwon. As for life in Seoul —
it was like a stress mark stamped
on some trivial sentence in my life.
Isn't Jochiwon a fairly big town itself?
Seoul was never my nest. Of course,
people from the provinces are all the more violent there.
Outside the dark train window, like fish bones floating in air,
winter trees stand startled and stark white.
For the branches of memory that once let birds fly free,
how many more seasons must they hold up their arms, struggling?
Even at the small tremor of the train slowing for a local stop,
people jolt awake. Their suspicious eyes,
laid bare like belongings on display,
close again,
and men toss and turn like dialects,
chasing after some more comfortable life.
At their feet, wretched dreams used to roll about like a few bread wrappers.
But Seoul is a good place. Because it teaches people
anger. Thanks to it, I've
done everything except stealing.
All the way to Jochiwon the man says nothing. What
is waiting for him there? I shake my head, wondering
how many times now has been his last homecoming.
My drowsiness, like a bad match, goes out again quickly.
Even if I happened to run into the man
on some Seoul street a few days later, so what. Everyone
keeps at least one coat on hand, for winter.

The man rises, small bag in hand. With the look of a firm zipper
his mouth opens just once to show a row of even teeth.
Walking toward the platform, the man
collides with some young men walking the other way.
The way people look when straining to hide some resolve,
the young men look as lonely as sawdust.
The man passes beneath a neon sign that reads Jochiwon.
And at that moment I see a large black bird. Surely
the man is flying slowly over the ground. The time is midnight.
Snow is falling.

Even without the shape of our mouths, we still communicate by mobilizing our eyes, foreheads, and our whole face. The value of so-called "nunchi" (reading the room through subtle cues) is growing, but even that isn't easy now that masks cover the area around the eyes too. Maybe that's why gestures are being used more than facial expressions these days, though they're harder to control as precisely as a face. Tone of voice gets mobilized too, but that also has its limits since masks muffle part of the voice. In particular, whispering or a low, soft tone and a smile — both effective at conveying emotion — are hard to get across through a mask. Because of masks, people end up having to raise their voices, and the mismatch between volume and content often creates an odd sense of dissonance.
Robert Fouser, Beyond an Age of Linguistic Distance
The point is that masks are having a major impact on how we use language. Just as the IMF crisis once completely reshaped our society's systems and ways of thinking, the use of masks will likely bring no small change to human life. As a middle-aged person, I recognize that time is a finite resource. So I'll try to free myself from pointless obsessions. Which means I won't make resolutions about absolutely finishing something within the year — that sort of thing suits graduate students writing their theses better. On the other hand, the things I can only do this year and never again, I will try to do this year. I don't want to be like the young man who puts off intimacy until age ninety for the sake of exam prep. Some things, if you don't do them in their season, you can never do at all. Apart from those things, I'll simply guard my daily routine. Every morning I'll boil an egg without fail, and once I've finished it I'll write that day's piece; in the afternoon I'll take a long walk. Along the way I'll stop at the coffee shop on my walking route for the day's coffee, and drop by the little bookshop kept by its taciturn owner to buy a book.

At times like this I find myself turning the word 'annyeonghi' (안녕히, 'safely/peacefully') over in my mind. It's supposed to mean 'comfortably, without any trouble or worry.' There must be more than one or two things you can do 'comfortably,' so what verbs does 'annyeonghi' actually pair with? (omitted)
'Stay well (annyeonghi gyeseyo).' 'Go well (annyeonghi gaseyo).' 'Sleep well (annyeonghi jumuseyo).' 'Go and come back safely (annyeonghi danyeoo-seyo).' If you really squeeze, maybe 'Return safely (annyeonghi doragaseyo).' So what's the problem, you ask? Just this: why can't we say 'Come safely (annyeonghi oseyo)'? Why does 'Rest well, play well, work well, eat well, watch well' — all with annyeonghi — sound so awkward?

I suppose annyeonghi is really the bare minimum courtesy we owe to someone who is leaving.

The video was filmed in Jeonbuk's Gimje, Juksan-myeon — once a bustling crossroads where a five-day market used to be held. But as a new highway opened, the village gradually lost its vitality. While preparing a special exhibition to trace the last hundred years of Seoul as reflected in popular songs — built around materials collected by pop-culture critic Choi Gyu-seong — the Cheonggyecheon Museum (director Kim Yeong-gwan) pulled together every popular song that used Seoul as its subject or theme, and came up with 1,141 songs in total, performed by 710 different singers.
Breaking it down further: 544 songs mentioned 'Seoul' directly in the title, 85 mentioned Myeong-dong, 70 mentioned the Han River, 55 mentioned Seoul Station, and 40 mentioned Namsan, among others. By singer, Na Hoon-a and Lee Mi-ja tied for first with 14 songs each, followed by Oh Gi-taek with 13, Seol Un-do with 12, and Domi and Yoon Il-ro with 11 each.
What started as a search for 'songs about Seoul' eventually led all the way to a 2010 exhibition at the Cheonggyecheon Museum, and later, to a published booklet. This is exactly the kind of microhistory we need more of.

1. FJ
FJs generally stay fairly calm and don't feel much when they're alone — at least until some outside trigger or problem stirs their emotions. Because of this, FJs might sometimes think of themselves as feeling "empty" or "indifferent."
They rarely make value judgments unless something dramatic happens out in the world.
FJs tend to see their own emotions as remarkably 'objective.' They observe other people's feelings closely, work hard to read subtle moods, and are strongly motivated to resolve conflict in relationships.
Of course, whether they do this 'well' depends on each FJ's own maturity, but since they at least put in the effort and genuinely enjoy doing it, they're more likely to be good at it. So generally speaking, FJs tend to read people more accurately than TPs and understand the subtle dynamics of relationships better.

Every language localizes. Even within a single language, all kinds of variation get mixed in — so once it crosses into another language, there's no way it stays exactly as it was. Language doesn't just struggle when it leaves home, it changes. English becomes Singlish in Singapore, Spanglish in Spain, Franglais in France, Konglish in Korea. The easiest place to spot it is in the vocabulary: 'handphone, car center, morning call, one-shot, back mirror (rearview mirror), remicon (remote control), autobike (motorcycle), sign (signature).' Even 'skinship' and 'fighting,' which have made it into the Oxford dictionary, are Konglish.
Kim Jin-hae, With Corona
The phrase used abroad — 'live with covid' and the like — came into Korea and settled as 'with corona.' The government reportedly decided to call it 'gradual return to daily life' instead, wherever possible, since 'with corona' might give the impression of disregarding new confirmed cases and doing away with social distancing altogether.
Setting aside the whole localization-versus-Konglish question, when I think about how to properly convey what a term actually implies, sometimes it's better not to simply go with the majority. For instance, the so-called 'Kim Young-ran Act' actually gets its meaning across better when called the 'Anti-Solicitation Act.' So personally, I'd rather say 'gradual return to daily life' than 'with corona.'

The single biggest reason KBS exists, as spelled out in Article 43, Paragraph 1 of the Broadcasting Act, is 'to establish a fair and healthy broadcasting culture and to efficiently carry out domestic and international broadcasting.' In other words, its reason for being is to make sure no one is unfairly excluded from broadcasting services — providing free service (beyond the basic license fee) to every household that owns a television, working to fix poor-reception areas, and guaranteeing equal access to information for the visually and hearing impaired through descriptive audio, captions, and sign-language broadcasts, turning all of that into the broadcasting standard. (...) That's precisely what citizens pay their license fee to KBS for, and in return KBS guarantees its employees a comfortable salary.
