Barthes, who was famously sensitive to weather, said in his final year of lectures at the Collège de France that weather is like the very essence of life and memory. Weather is a kind of blank state, a meaninglessness that lets us communicate and make contact with one another — and precisely because of that, it can hold subtle nuances words can't capture, or so the idea goes. Put another way, it may be weather itself that produces those delicate nuances. 
Thanks to COVID-19 (in this case 'thanks to' really is the right phrase, not 'because of'), September 2021 has brought us the clearest autumn skies imaginable. Instagram is flooded with photos of sky and clouds. 
Sitting beneath a persimmon tree, I imagine sunlight occasionally falling on my forehead, carried by a gentle breeze. I think I understand now why weather is the essence of life and memory.

Ignorance is not something to mock. Who would even dare? But if that ignorance is the result of contempt, that’s a different matter — if a callousness toward historical violence and the wounds it inflicted on humanity is what grants us permission to remain ignorant. Praising 120-hour work weeks is contempt for the wounds left by a history of labor exploitation; pride in national ceremony is contempt for the unhappy history of nationalism that forced individuals into sacrifice; approaching the nuclear phase-out purely as an industrial issue is contempt for the tragedy humanity suffered through nuclear accidents. Ignorance as contempt like this becomes violence against every victim, past and present. What kind of learning do we need now? It is time to study how to protect others from ourselves. We must protect others from our own ignorance.
If learning in the past meant learning to protect myself from myself, and to protect myself from others, then this is a time that calls for learning how to protect others from my own ignorance.

'The flight crew has the final authority, always'
'All humans make mistakes'
The former is Boeing's philosophy, the latter is Airbus's. Both are baked directly into how their planes are engineered - for instance, Boeing's aircraft are designed so that, under normal circumstances where you'd never need to bank the wings past 90 degrees anyway, the pilot can still override and adjust the angle at their own judgment. Airbus, on the other hand, is built so that even if the pilot gives a command, the computer analyzes it first and only executes it within limits it judges aerodynamically safe.
Organizations and individuals alike operate and act based on some such philosophy or principle. But a philosophy or principle is the result of a long process of trial and error. Much like today's strict aviation regulations, which exist because of countless accidents and lives lost. It's often said, after all, that every aviation regulation is written in blood.

퀴노아치커리샐러드-모닝리추얼-모닝루틴.ingredients: 1 serving chicory, 1/4 paprika, 1/4 onion, 1 cup quinoa, a handful of pecans, (dressing) 3T olive oil, 1T lemon juice, 1t maple syrup, olive oil, salt and pepper, a little herbs
퀴노아치커리샐러드-모닝리추얼-모닝루틴.steps:
1. Rinse the chicory and paprika in clean water, then cut into bite-sized pieces. 
2. Slice the onion into long strips and soak briefly in water. 
3. Rinse the quinoa once, then combine quinoa and water in a 1:2 ratio in a pot; once it comes to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it steam for 5 minutes to finish. 
4. Plate the chicory, paprika, onion, and the quinoa from step 3, then drizzle with dressing. 
5. Toast the pecans in a pan, chop, and sprinkle over the salad.

단호박스프-모닝리추얼-모닝루틴.steps:

When planning events big or small, I take the background music pretty seriously. Last week I had to put together a small farewell gathering, and on a colleague's advice, I agonized over it and picked 'Let's Not Forget' (Jang Pil-sun, Kim Hyun-chul)—(there's a Sung Si-kyung/Kwon Jina version too, but somehow it had to be this one). 
Quietly pleased with my song choice, I was running through it in rehearsal when I remembered giving up on practicing this very song ahead of a performance a long time ago. Right before the emotionally soaring chorus line—"though our meeting ends here now~"—the rhythm, unlike the rest of the song, is deeply strange. 
I don't mean to disparage this beautiful song. But for someone with no sense of rhythm, that phrase, which hesitates as if it's about to land and then lands half a beat—or a quarter beat—off, can only be described, regrettably, as 'strange.' And anyone who's rhythmically challenged will agree with this completely. Though this is a story that has no place in the breakfast universe.

The generational theory getting attention lately can be summed up like this: men in their 20s and 30s are, relatively speaking, less inclined than people in their 50s or women in their 20s and 30s to want to share what they have with the disadvantaged in our society. Chronos is time in its ordinary sense: the natural time that simply flows on whether we do anything or not — calendar time, objective time. It's a concept of time given equally to everyone.
Kairos is conscious, subjective time — the time of opportunity and decision, when a single choice in the moment can shape a life. It's the meaning we assign within the Chronos we're all given equally. (Isn't there such a thing as a minute that feels like an hour, and an hour that feels like a minute?)

There's a South African proverb that also appears in the lyrics of a popular song there: 'Umuntu ngumuntu ngubantu.' It means 'a person is only a person through other people.' 
I read that line in a book I've been going through lately. It's a kind of ontology — the idea that I only take on meaning through you, the other who is not me.

This is all about non-fungible tokens (NFTs). The idea is to store ownership of a digital file on the blockchain so it can never be forged or altered and is preserved permanently, with that ownership verifiable in a decentralized way — but put simply, it's just a 'digital certificate of authenticity.' 
I remember, a very long time ago, sitting in a sunlit corner of a library, carefully turning the yellowed pages (afraid they might tear) of Walter Benjamin's 'The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction.' 한성우-말의주인이되는시간-한글.title: Han Seong-woo, Becoming the Master of Your Words, and Hangul

These days, young people are trying something new. In the past, a word might have been coined from Chinese characters, but now people build words purely out of Hangul. If you needed a word for 'a meal eaten at home,' someone comfortable with Chinese characters might have coined gasik (家食) or gaban (家飯), but people today simply shorten it to jipbap ('house rice'). Likewise, 'eating alone' or 'traveling alone' might once have been dokban (獨飯) or dokhaeng (獨行), but now they're simply honbap and honhaeng. (...) It's a clever choice that really understands what Hangul is good at.
Thanks to Hangul, and to how self-sufficient Hangul is, today's breakfast has a name — otherwise I might have had to call it xihongshi chao jidan.

Someone else caught that line immediately and pushed back: 'Are you trying to start a fight? There's clearly a difference between "rear end" and "backside."' When a cost-cutting government policy cut off any way to reach her family on a planet tens of thousands of light-years away, she used deep-freezing to extend her own life by over a hundred years, never letting go of her dream of one day meeting her family again — even though they would surely already be dead by then.

Would you say goodbye to your family, friends, and colleagues and go to sleep? Or would you choose to accept the incurable illness as it is, right now? 20210116
I recall reading #LeeOdeok's #WritingOurLanguageCorrectly quite a while ago, and one part has stuck with me:
The word 'geunyeo' ('she'), which doesn't originally exist in Korean, is a translation of the Japanese word 'kanojo' (彼女), so there's really no need to distinguish 'he' from 'she' in Korean the way it forces us to. In everyday speech, people just say 'geu saram' ('that person') and rarely bother with 'geunyeo.' 'That kid,' 'that woman,' 'that lady,' or simply 'he/that one' works just fine.
On top of that, it still bothers me a little that saying 'geunyeo' conjures up an image of a woman with long straight hair and pale skin. (Maybe it's just me.) Anyway, thanks to that book, I've come to enjoy using the gender-neutral 'geu,' and it makes me happy whenever I meet someone else who does the same.
Heat olive oil in a pan and blanch the prettiest asparagus in the world. Add a little salt and pepper if you like. Also lightly reheat some broccoli I'd pre-boiled. Drizzle with dressing right before eating.

Yogurt +10 days, eggs +25 days, milk +45 days, tofu +90 days, cheese +70 days, cooking oil +5 years, canned tuna +10 years...
'Sell-by date' refers to the legal deadline by which a distributor is allowed to sell a product on the market. 'Use-by date,' on the other hand, refers to the final date by which a food is still considered safe to eat.
According to Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the Korea Consumer Agency, a product's actual use-by date typically runs anywhere from 5 to over 50 days past its printed sell-by date. Barring special cases, thinking in terms of use-by dates rather than just sell-by dates can be a small kindness to the planet. Today's overripe avocado is a good example.

바이센테니얼맨-아이로봇-아이작아시모프.title: Bicentennial Man, I, Robot, and Isaac Asimov
바이센테니얼맨-아이로봇-아이작아시모프.intro:
20210113
There's such a thing as the Three Laws of Robotics — the operating principles for robots that #IsaacAsimov, the original author behind films like #BicentennialMan and #IRobot, laid out in his own work.
1. A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm.
2. A robot must obey any orders given by human beings, except where such orders would conflict with the First Law.
3. A robot must protect its own existence, except where doing so would conflict with the First or Second Law.
A Korean AI startup's chatbot, 'Iruda,' ran into trouble after it absorbed users' distorted views on gender and outright hate speech, and the service was eventually suspended. According to its developers, Iruda is like a small child who has only just begun talking with people, and still has a lot to learn. We should give some grace to the trial and error that comes with technological progress, but when you consider how the public actually trains AI, it's worth thinking more carefully about what effect that might have on people.
There's a lot to think carefully about these days. Luckily, today's breakfast doesn't require any careful thought at all — grilled green onions, ready in 10 minutes. They say winter scallions are as good as a tonic.
Heat olive oil in a pan and grill the scallions. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Blanch a sausage in boiling water, then finish it with a quick sear in the pan alongside the scallions.

월레스앤그로밋-양털도둑-오트밀.intro:

In #WallaceAndGromit's #ACloseShave, Wallace has a launcher for quick breakfast oatmeal (or more precisely, porridge — oatmeal thickened with soy milk and the like). The problem is it works a little too well. As a result, the launcher later ends up doubling as a weapon for catching the villain. Honestly, isn't that basically #CES2021-level tech?
Pour cashew soy milk over oatmeal, mix in chia seeds, cinnamon, honey, and cherries that have been soaking in Havana rum, and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, take out the overnight oats that have set overnight and eat them (today) with blueberries on top.

나의프랑스식조식.title: My French-Style Breakfast

Built around 11 themes — 5G, IoT, autonomous driving, blockchain, health, robotics, advertising, and more — the show is set to unveil new cross-industry concept services: Samsung Electronics and Harman's Digital Cockpit 2021, which aims to turn the inside of a car into a third living space; Amorepacific's AI-powered beauty service; GS Caltex's gas station of the future; and more.

굿모닝에브리원-레이첼맥아담스-해리슨포드.title: Morning Glory, Rachel McAdams, and Harrison Ford
굿모닝에브리원-레이첼맥아담스-해리슨포드.intro:
After being fired from a local station and landing a hard-won job at a major network, Becky (Rachel McAdams) is put in charge of 'Daybreak,' the lowest-rated morning show around. To boost ratings, she brings in legendary anchor Mike Pomeroy, but the two clash over everything.
'The beauty of a frittata is that you can make it with whatever's in the fridge.'
Early one morning, ahead of a big broadcast, Mike (Harrison Ford) makes a frittata for Becky, who's pulled an all-nighter. It's the moment the stubborn, legendary anchor's heart finally begins to open.

직장인-중식-점심밥.title: Office Worker's Midday Lunch
직장인-중식-점심밥.intro:
20210108-2
A few years back, a book called Dictators' Dinners was published in the UK, profiling the dishes that won over the palates of dictators like Saddam Hussein, Kim Jong-il, and Stalin. Hitler, known as a vegetarian, apparently enjoyed things like 'in-season asparagus with Hollandaise sauce made from butter, egg yolk, and vinegar, vegetable soup, roasted salad, and vegetable stew.'
Thanks to an unplanned day of working from home, I made asparagus gratin for lunch, and even without actual Hollandaise sauce, it somehow gave off the same vibe as what Hitler reportedly enjoyed — especially paired with the broccoli soup I'd had for breakfast.
-Boil lasagna sheets in water, drain, and lay them on the bottom of the dish. (Really, I should have brushed them with olive oil first.)
-Arrange the prettiest asparagus in the world neatly on top, then add cream sauce, chopped prosciutto, and Gruyère cheese. (Really, I should have used ham instead of prosciutto, and mixed Greek yogurt into the cream sauce.)
-Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, then pepper pepper pepper pepper pepper.
*The cream sauce is made by melting butter in a pan, then whisking in flour and milk. Making it brought back memories of when I was devoted to baking, long ago — it's been over a decade.
*I've been working my way through the recipes in #MyFrenchSalads and #MyFrenchOvenDishes, one at a time. It's a really good book.

메로나-직장인-조식.title: Melona, and an Office Worker's Breakfast
메로나-직장인-조식.intro:

'We kept the color the same green as melon, but developed the flavor closer to Korean melon (chamoe), and consumer response was explosive.' Back in the 1980s, for consumers who weren't used to the taste of actual melon, Binggrae's marketing team's answer was 'a melon-colored ice pop that tastes closer to Korean melon' — Melona. #Melona
I remember laughing to myself when I learned that crab-flavored sticks are actually made from Alaska pollock, and that banana-flavored milk doesn't actually contain banana. I recall there being some controversy for a while over chamoe-flavored Melona. Moral absolutists like Kant, who believed lying is always wrong, would probably have been outraged if they were alive today — but really, it's just 'crab-flavored' sticks and 'banana-flavored' milk.
Oh, and apparently chamoe goes by 'Korean Melon' in English-speaking countries. Anyway, today's breakfast isn't melon-flavored — it's the real thing.
-Scoop out the melon's seeds, then scoop the flesh with a measuring spoon since I don't have a melon baller.
(Scooped melon flesh releases a lot of juice, so it's best to drain it in a sieve before plating.)
-Arrange the mozzarella pearls and prosciutto together nicely.
-Pepper pepper pepper pepper, then drizzle with balsamic right before eating.

괴식-직장인-조식.title: A Weird Little Breakfast, Office Worker Style
괴식-직장인-조식.intro:

No time to make gnocchi from scratch, so I buy it ready-made. It looks nice and it's cheap. Best of all, the recipe doesn't call for heavy cream, which makes it a great fit for breakfast.
-Blanch the gnocchi in boiling water with a little olive oil.
-Drain well in a sieve, then pan-fry with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
-Add the prettiest boiled green peas in the world, a little butter, parsley flakes, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Finish with parmesan~

직장인-조식-아침밥.title: An Office Worker's Morning Meal
직장인-조식-아침밥.intro:
20210105
Honestly, there's no shortage of debates like this. Honey or soy sauce on rice cake? Fried or seasoned chicken? When making ramyeon, soup base first or noodles first? Wheat rice cakes or rice-flour rice cakes in tteokbokki? Who do you love more, mom or dad?
Here's another one: a scone spread jam-then-cream, versus a scone spread cream-then-jam. This is the age-old cream tea debate between England's Devon and Cornwall, each claiming to be the true birthplace of cream tea. (Jam then cream is the Cornwall camp; cream then jam is the Devon camp.)
Meanwhile, according to mathematician Eugenia Cheng's analysis (which might just settle this pointless debate once and for all):
-The ratio of scone to jam to cream (or cream to jam) should be 2:1:1, and
-For the best flavor, you should build the layers like a sandcastle. To pull that off, density naturally dictates that jam goes on first, then cream.
*Cream tea is a simplified version of afternoon tea — scones spread with clotted cream and jam, served alongside tea.
*This post is based on brunch writer @chovin's post, 'The Cream Tea Debate — The British Version of Dip vs. Pour.'

A senior colleague introduced me to this musician years ago, and I even once sang his song 'A Thoughtful Night' at a concert. This morning's paper ran a piece titled 'Year of the Ox: Artists Who Plod Along Steadily,' and seeing him mentioned there brought the memory back, so on my first commute of the new year, I listen to his song.

Radicchio and tangerine salad

포테이토스킨-감자-고구마.title: Potato Skins with Potato and Sweet Potato
포테이토스킨-감자-고구마.intro:
20200103
Potato varieties fall into two types: mealy potatoes, which are great for frying or steaming, and waxy potatoes, best for soups and stir-fries. Most potatoes grown in Korea today are the waxy type, which is why fast-food chains like McDonald's import mealy potatoes from abroad for their fries. Back in the Japanese colonial period, apparently, a mealy American variety called 'Danshaku' (Irish Cobbler), brought in through Japan, was widely eaten — and that's actually the origin of Gangwon-do's old native potato. Anyway, the point is that potato skins with that supposedly amazing crispy texture are hard to pull off with waxy potatoes. So as I ate my not-so-crispy, somewhat mealy-textured potato skins, I made up this long excuse. (Source: Namu Wiki)
-Cut potato and sweet potato in half and steam them. Let cool slightly, then scoop out the flesh. Brush evenly with olive oil, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and bake at 210°C for 10 minutes.
-Fill the potato and sweet potato skins with cheese, parsley, and jamón, then bake again at 210°C for another 10 minutes. (Used mozzarella since I was out of cheddar.)
-Top with the prettiest sour cream in the world, made the day before, and enjoy.
*The prettiest sour cream in the world = heavy cream and yogurt in a 3:1 ratio, with 2 to 3 T of lemon juice stirred in well, left to ferment at room temperature for about 6 hours, then refrigerated overnight.

The heroine Helena Campbell travels — together with her uncles and the science geek (that's the only way to describe him) they've picked out as her fiancé — to see the green ray, said to keep her from being fooled by feelings of love (in other words, to let her recognize true love when she sees it). After a long and winding journey she falls in love along the way with the hero, Olivier Sinclair. At the end of the trip, not a short one, the group finally witnesses the green ray. #JulesVerne #TheGreenRay

뭐라고-머라고-직장인.title: Oyster & Chicory Salad

According to the National Institute of Korean Language's Twitter, apparently '뭐라고' (mworago, "what did you say") can also be written as '머라고' (meorago). The reasoning: '머' is a colloquial way of saying '뭐' ("what"), used in phrases like "Are you eating something (머) by yourself?" or "What (머) do you like, sis?" 
A truly shocking, absurd fact for people who can't rest easy until they've corrected even the smallest spelling typo in an ordinary KakaoTalk message.

길티플레저-을지OB베어-노가리골목.intro:
20201227, This year's #GuiltyPleasure is ____________. 
After working late, around 9:30 pm, it's better not to eat dinner yet. On the way home, I change direction at Euljiro 3(sam)-ga station and head for #EuljiroOBBear. You have to grab a seat in that tiny, two-or-three-pyeong room. In this neighborhood's #NogariAlley, the #unwrittenrule is a draft beer and dried pollock as the default, but I order a draft beer with sausage and halfbeak instead. The old proprietor always follows up with, 'Didn't eat dinner, did you?' I put in my AirPods and pull out a book. Classical music with no lyrics is best. One page per sip of draft beer poured without any rapid-chill gadget, and a bite of sausage or halfbeak. If I have a second glass, it's dried filefish instead of halfbeak. But never more than two glasses. It's perfect alone, though if I have a dear friend along, two of us works too. Never three. Since the place closes at 11, I get up around 10:30 with last orders in mind. Stepping out the door, I always check my shadow under the streetlight. #2020YearEndReview #EuljiroOBBear 
This year's guilty pleasure is drinking alone at Euljiro OB Bear. I dropped by especially often early in the year — these days, who knows when I'll get to go back.

연말정산-나의프랑스식샐러드-나의프랑스식오븐요리.intro:

In that spirit, My French-Style Salad is easily one of my books of the year. Since My French-Style Oven Dishes just came out, I jumped straight in and tried an oven breakfast — not exactly easy on a weekday.

-Plate it, sprinkle with salt, pepper, and parsley, then tear prosciutto by hand and add on top.

Red onion and onion roasted well in the oven have an incredible sweetness. Pick up a piece, top it with prosciutto, and your mouth fills with a luxurious sweet-and-salty flavor.

20201225-세상에서-제일-예쁜-녹색의-아스파라거스와-빨간색의-토마.title: Christmas Tree Salad: Asparagus & Tomato

에쿠니가오리-츠지히토나리-냉정과열정사이.title: Cold and Passion Between Us: Open Sandwich
에쿠니가오리-츠지히토나리-냉정과열정사이.intro:
20201224, I don't know. I don't know when, or how much, one is supposed to open up. Some people left tired because I never opened up enough; some were startled off because I opened up too soon. Whether by chance or by necessity, here we all are now, like a small miracle built out of hard choices and everything that followed from them. I find myself thinking about opening up more. And fittingly, today's breakfast is an 'open' sandwich.

나무위키-채식주의자-동물권.title: The Vegetarian & Animal Rights: Tempeh Breakfast
나무위키-채식주의자-동물권.intro:
20201223, Through fragments of memory and dreams, Yeong-hye comes to realize she is someone with 'living things stuck in her throat, choking her.' What starts as a revulsion toward meat grows into a rejection of violence against life itself, and in the end she struggles to transcend her own existence as an animal that can only survive by killing other living things. #NamuWiki #TheVegetarian
I'm no vegan myself, but I do lean toward vegetables over meat. People come to veganism for all kinds of reasons — religion, ethics, the environment, personal trauma — and if I ever did choose that path, I suspect it would be for environmental reasons rather than the question of life itself that haunts Yeong-hye in The Vegetarian. #AnimalRights
A very simple vegan breakfast today. I thaw some black bean #tempeh I bought last week at #Marche in water for a bit, then sear it in a pan with a little olive oil. They say all kinds of sauces go well with it, but today it's #srirachasauce
*Tempeh is an Indonesian food made by fermenting beans — closer to cheonggukjang than to tofu. The beans are soaked, hulled, lightly cooked, then fermented for several days with a mold called Rhizopus. As the mycelium grows in between the beans it binds them into a firm block that's not only high in protein but rich in saponins, isoflavones, amino acids, vitamins, and dietary fiber. (Source: Maison Korea)

스포티파이-애자일-애자일하게.title: Overnight Oats: The Agile Breakfast
스포티파이-애자일-애자일하게.intro:
20201222, News that #Spotify, the world's biggest music streaming service, is finally launching in Korea. Who is Spotify, exactly? A company built on the philosophy that 'the only real cure for illegal downloads is a free service,' one that casually outmaneuvered even Steve Jobs's Apple Music to stand at the top of the global streaming market. Thanks to that, you have to sit through ads you don't want — unless, like on YouTube, you pay a monthly fee to skip them. 
Spotify is actually a company that comes up constantly whenever people talk about #Agile. Its flexible internal collaboration and learning-driven approach to innovation almost read as the textbook definition of agile. What struck me most, though, was hearing that by the time the outside world catches on to 'this is how Spotify does things,' Spotify itself has already moved on to something else. That's probably the whole essence of agile. 
*By the dictionary, #agile simply means nimble or quick-moving; in practice it's also a methodology and philosophy centered on constant change and innovation, unbound by traditional ways of doing things. 
Soak your oats the night before and you can start the next morning very #agile-ly. This is #OvernightOats. 
-Add 3-4 spoonfuls of #oats to a suitable container and pour in #cashewmilk.
-Mix in cranberries, chia seeds, honey, and cinnamon, then refrigerate. 
The next morning, scoop out a portion and top with fruit like blueberries or strawberries. A truly #agile morning.

반숙계란-방울양배추-아스파라거스.title: Soft-Boiled Egg, Brussels Sprouts & Asparagus
반숙계란-방울양배추-아스파라거스.intro:
20201221, Today is the winter solstice — the longest night (and shortest day) of the year in the northern hemisphere. From today onward, the nights grow shorter and the days gradually longer. The hardships and trials symbolized by the long night will slowly fade, and soon a day, a daylight, of hope will arrive. 
So let's all eat a hearty breakfast together and greet the solstice sun with full energy. 
Drizzle olive oil in a pan and sear the boiled Brussels sprouts and asparagus. Plate them together with a soft-boiled egg and finish with a dressing of olive oil, whole-grain mustard, and white wine vinegar. 
#SoftBoiledEgg know-how
-Put the eggs in a pan or pot and pour in water until they're about half submerged. Cover with a lid and cook on the highest heat for 5 minutes. 
-Turn off the heat and let sit for another 5 minutes. 
-Transfer the eggs into cold water and leave for about 5 minutes. 
The exact timing varies stove to stove, but this should get you a soft-boiled egg.

오명돈-지속가능한방역에대한어느의사의질문-방울다다기양배추.title: A Doctor's Question on Sustainable Quarantine: Brussels Sprouts
오명돈-지속가능한방역에대한어느의사의질문-방울다다기양배추.intro:
20201220, When Ebola broke out in Africa in 2014, a lot of people lost their lives. Ebola is a disease where the virus is present in every bodily fluid. In traditional African funeral customs, the family fully washes and prepares the body of the deceased themselves. Because the virus is so potent, many family members ended up dying again through the funeral itself — the funeral became a kind of amplification event. So authorities banned the funerals, and there were sound medical reasons for it. Even so, for the people there, that was a duty owed to their children, a funeral culture, even at the risk of infection. 
What makes COVID-19 so hard to bear is that it forces us to act against things that are matters of duty and culture. A green, green breakfast to soothe a crowded mind. 
Blanch the world's prettiest #brusselssprouts, #greenbeans, and #broccoli in #bubbling boiling water, drain, and plate. Drizzle on a dressing of olive oil, whole-grain mustard, and white wine vinegar, then grate parmesan over the top. 
This morning I also poured a cup of milk, microwaved it in three 30-second bursts, then pump-pump-pump-pump-pump-pumped by hand to make plenty of #steamedmilk, poured it over #espresso, and had myself a #caffelatte too.

에린핸슨-아닌것-나조식.title: Erin Hanson's What You Are Not: Yum Woon Sen
에린핸슨-아닌것-나조식.intro:
20201219, 
Your age is not you
Nor the size of the clothes you wear
Nor your weight
Nor the color of your hair

Your name is not you
Nor the dimples in your cheeks
You are every book you have read
And every word you speak

You are the rasp in your voice each morning
And the smile you couldn't quite hide
You are the loveliness inside your laughter
And every tear you've cried

You are the song you sing at the top of your lungs
When you know you are utterly alone
The places you have traveled to
And the place you call home

You are the things you believe in
And the people that you love
The photographs hung on your walls
And the future you dream of

You are made of so many beautiful things
But it seems you forget
In the moment you decide
To define yourself by everything you are not

(#ErinHanson #WhatYouAreNot)
If I can add one more line: you are the food you've eaten, the breakfast you've had
(#najosik #WhatsOutside)
The cilantro I bought last week at #Marche is still fresh — I wrapped it well in a damp kitchen towel. So it's #YamWoonsen again. 
-Slice celery, onion, and tomato into a bowl. Finely chop the world's prettiest #cilantro and some scallion. (No chives on hand.)
-Blanch the glass noodles (made from konjac) in boiling water and drain, then — no need to boil fresh water — blanch the squid, shrimp, and ground pork in the same pot. 
-Toss everything with a dressing of fish sauce, palm sugar, lime juice, a little minced garlic, and 2 crushed peperoncino peppers. 
-Top with a little peanuts and cilantro.

마르쉐-밤아저씨밤-생율샐러드.title: Marché Chestnut Man's Chestnuts: Raw Chestnut Salad
마르쉐-밤아저씨밤-생율샐러드.intro:
20201218, The era of typing away diligently on a laptop at the office is over — that's something you can just as well do at home. The exciting part is that the purpose of going to the office from now on will be to generate ideas and collaborate with colleagues. (Dale Sinclair, 'The Normalization of Remote Work,' on the future of offices that COVID-19 will reshape) 
When will ordinary things like going out to eat with coworkers, or grabbing a drink after work, be possible again? Ten years from now, how will we remember this period? Will going to the office become simply a space for generating ideas and collaborating with colleagues? I thought about all this while finely julienning chestnuts. 
These are #ChestnutManChestnuts, bought last weekend at #Marche. 
-Julienne the world's prettiest chestnuts and jujubes, and roughly chop the walnuts. 
-Toss the chopped ingredients together with a dressing of honey (1), sugar (1/2), olive oil (1), white wine vinegar (1), and a little salt. #RawChestnutSalad
#officeworker #breakfast #breakfastmeal #breakfasttable #salad #chestnutsalad #rawchestnutsalad #breakfast #chestnut #chestnutsalad *Referenced Naver's Every:Mom blog, 'The Start of Every Dish.'

일의기쁨과슬픔-장류진-일확천금.title: Jang Ryu-jin & the Get-Rich-Quick Dream: Broccoli Salad
일의기쁨과슬픔-장류진-일확천금.intro:
20201217, 'A salary alone isn't enough — what we need is a windfall.' That tagline hooked me from the start, and when I found out it was by Jang Ryu-jin, author of The Joy and Sorrow of Work — my (Na Jo-sik's) pick for best book of 2020 — and that a new chapter drops online every week? There was no reason to hesitate. Go read it right now! 
Just google 'Jang Ryu-jin To the Moon' — currently updated through chapter 7!
I should have caught on from the 'windfall' tagline: To the Moon features, unsurprisingly, the #cryptocurrency that once had our whole society fired up. Fittingly, yesterday #Bitcoin broke its all-time high, crossing $20,000. (Though, to be fair, To the Moon centers on #Ethereum rather than Bitcoin — at least through chapter 7.) 
But today's breakfast has nothing to do with cryptocurrency: it's broccoli salad. Blanch the world's prettiest broccoli in boiling water, drizzle with a dressing of whole-grain mustard, white wine vinegar, and olive oil, and finish with parmesan~

어제의한장면-직장인-조식.title: A Scene from Yesterday: Prosciutto Bruschetta
어제의한장면-직장인-조식.intro:
20201216, With a confirmed COVID case forcing everyone out of the office in a hurry, the place looked just like a scene from a disaster film — you know the kind, where people vanish in an instant for some unknown reason. At one desk, a half-written Post-it and a pen sat abandoned; across from it, a computer screen still showed an email with no recipient filled in. In the empty seats, phones rang like short, startled screams, over and over, and cold air blew in through a window someone had left open for ventilation. The morning news said the daily COVID-19 case count had topped a thousand for the first time, and that it was the coldest day of the winter so far. Out the window, far off, I could see coworkers huddled together in small groups against the cold, collars turned up, heading toward the temporary screening clinic offering free COVID tests. #ASceneFromYesterday
And so, this breakfast post ends up posted late, as it goes. 
I threw together — at the speed of light — a bruschetta of bread topped with basil pesto, the world's prettiest chicory, and prosciutto, and ate it.

크림티논쟁-괴식-당근수프.title: The Cream Tea Debate & a Food Fail: Carrot Soup
크림티논쟁-괴식-당근수프.intro:
20201215, I originally meant to bring up the British equivalent of the dip-first-or-dunk-first debate — the #CreamTeaDebate between the Cornwall and Devon camps — and imagined an elegant breakfast of clotted cream and carrot soup. 
But when I opened the tub, there was almost no clotted cream left. I tried to improvise — butter over jam, jam over butter — but concluded this counted as a #foodfail, and disqualified it from the post. More than anything, I'm reminded once again that trying more than one dish during the busy morning rush is asking too much. So today's breakfast is simply #CarrotSoup
-Melt butter in a pan and sauté half an onion until translucent. Then add the carrot, cut into half-moons, and sauté as well. 
-Add the world's prettiest chickpeas, boiled the night before, pour in a little water and a good amount of milk, and simmer for 2-3 minutes. 
-Pour into a blender and puree. 
-Transfer back to the pot and (since there's no whipping cream) simmer again with a bit more milk added. 
*It comes out the color of pumpkin soup, overwhelmingly thanks to the chickpeas. #CarrotsAreJustTheSidekick

보노보노-관자-키조개관자버터구이.title: Bono Bono: Butter-Seared Scallops
보노보노-관자-키조개관자버터구이.intro:
20201214, If you're looking for something, you can't afford to lose your way — get confused even once, and you may never find it again. But it's okay to get confused, too, because something else will turn up. #BonoBono 
Year-end, so many things left to wrap up. Which makes for an especially heavy Monday. On top of that, daily confirmed cases have topped a thousand, and Level 3 social distancing looms. But like Bono Bono says, 'something else will turn up.' As thanks to Bono Bono for the comfort and small wisdom he's given me, I offer him a breakfast of his favorite item — the razor clam (scallop) he's always clutching. Or wait, was that actually a scallop? Ha.
-Score the scallops, season lightly with salt and pepper (skipping the mirin, since I'm out), and let sit briefly. 
-Melt butter in a pan and sear the scallops on low heat, briefly on each side, along with the world's prettiest green beans, and mushrooms and garlic if you like. 
-Plate and grate parmigiano over the top. In an instant, the breakfast's whole standing shoots up.

최승자-마흔-첫눈.title: Choi Seung-ja's Forty: First Snow Gnocchi Salad
최승자-마흔-첫눈.intro:
20201213, 
When I turned thirty, I felt like I was standing at the edge of a high cliff,
as if every step from then on
would be an endless plunge down a steep slope.

But my forties turned out to be a vast, vaulted plain,
endlessly wide — walk and walk
and no wall, no downhill slope ever comes into view.
Except that everywhere there are invisible glass walls,
where, if your luck is bad, you smack your head into one with a thud.

And yet there is exactly one thing I still believe in,
so in this fortieth year, every single day, the axe I trust in cuts my own foot.
Memory is selfish. I read this poem a very long time ago and believed that once I turned 'forty,' I'd shake off whatever struggles I was facing at the time and stand fully enlightened atop that vast plain. Turns out I only remembered half of it. Now that I've lived it, even at forty the struggles — like those 'invisible glass walls' — are still very much there, and I go on bruising my head, sometimes my little toe, against them. So then, what's the one thing I believe in that could soothe that kind of pain? Does it even exist?

Boil gnocchi in salted water, drain, and toss in olive oil. Sear tomato and enoki mushrooms in a pan with olive oil. Arrange the world's prettiest chicory, red onion, and prosciutto with the prepared gnocchi, tomato, and enoki mushrooms, then grate parmigiano cheese over the top, quietly, gently, like the #FirstSnow. Finish with a light drizzle of whole-grain mustard, white wine vinegar, and olive oil dressing. 
Thinking about it, I suppose what I believe in these days might just be (my) breakfast.

들깨가래떡-조식.title: Perilla Rice Cake Breakfast
들깨가래떡-조식.intro:
20201212, The myths handed down to us never fail to include a stern lesson and warning for humans who destroy forests. The Epic of Gilgamesh, said to be the oldest story in human history, tells of a flood that strikes after the gods' forest is destroyed; in the Book of Genesis, humans who touch the tree of life are cast out of Eden. The myth of humanity's exile from paradise for disturbing forests and trees turns out to be our own situation too. (Kim Min-sik, The Time of Trees)
The cause still hasn't been confirmed, but there's a theory that COVID-19 emerged when bats, driven from their habitats by deforestation, came into contact with humans. Others predict that deforestation, through a chain reaction, is melting polar permafrost and could release ancient viruses that have lain dormant inside it, posing an ongoing threat to human survival. Perhaps the day humanity gets exiled from this planet for disturbing its trees is drawing steadily closer. 
Today, let's each quietly, slowly, go digging through the deep, frozen corners of our own fridge for something to eat. #PerillaRiceCake #breakfast

가는날이장날-얌운센.title: Bad Timing, Good Luck: Yum Woon Sen
가는날이장날-얌운센.intro:
20201211, I rushed, out of breath, to the store right before closing to buy breakfast ingredients — and of course the one thing missing was exactly what I needed. On the day of an all-company outdoor event that had taken considerable effort to organize, with hundreds attending, a fine-dust advisory (not even a warning, an outright ban on outdoor activity) kept absurdly going off. 
The Korean expression 'the day you go is market day' (bad timing, missed connection) comes from a story about going to great trouble to visit a faraway friend, only to find the village happened to be holding its market that very day, so the friend was out and about, and you had no choice but to turn back without seeing them. These days, though, people apparently also use the phrase when things unexpectedly work out really well. #BadTimingGoodLuck
This Yum Woon Sen, thrown together in a hurry after I couldn't buy the breakfast ingredients I'd planned for, turns out to be exactly that kind of lucky bad timing. This is the precise verdict of Na Jo-sik, who judges a Thai restaurant's real skill by its yum woon sen and has probably eaten a thousand bowls of it by now. 
Slice celery, onion, and tomato into a bowl, and add lightly blanched squid and shrimp. (Wanted to add chives and ground pork too, but skipped them since I was out.)
Blanch the glass noodles briefly in boiling water, drain, and add to the bowl, then toss with a dressing of fish sauce, lime juice, a little minced garlic, and peperoncino. Top with a little peanuts and cilantro. 
*Yam means to mix/toss, and woon sen refers to vermicelli — glass noodles made from mung bean starch. Swapping in konjac noodles for the vermicelli barely changes the texture.

직장인뫼비우스의띠-새우메밀국수샐러드-메밀국수.title: The Office Worker's Möbius Strip: Shrimp Buckwheat Noodle Salad
직장인뫼비우스의띠-새우메밀국수샐러드-메밀국수.intro:
20201210, 1) 'If you don't know, ask' -> 2) you ask -> 3) 'You still don't know that?' -> 4) you stop asking -> back to 1
1) 'Do you really need to be told everything?' -> 2) you use your own judgment -> 3) 'Why'd you just decide that on your own?' -> 4) you go passive -> back to 1
A story that circulates under the name #TheOfficeWorkersMobiusStrip — something that crossed my mind after watching a batch of passionate job applicants the other day. Fellow seniors, life is one long string of trial and error; let's not do this to them. 
The world of breakfast is no different — it takes at least three rounds of trial and error before the taste and look come together properly. This is only my second attempt at shrimp buckwheat noodle salad, so I figure it'll come together better next time. Boil the buckwheat noodles, drain, rinse in cold water, then toss with a little olive oil and salt. Sear the shrimp in a pan with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then slice cucumber thin with a peeler and wrap it snugly around the shrimp before laying it over the noodles. Drizzle with a dressing of olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard, and enjoy.

호불호-호불호조식-직장인.title: Love It or Hate It: Office Worker's Breakfast
호불호-호불호조식-직장인.intro:
20201209, Level 1: what do these drinks have in common? Maccol, Dejawa, Sol's Pine Needle, Dr Pepper, Denmark Milk's mint latte, mint choco milk
Level 2: what do these vegetables have in common? Cucumber, cilantro, eggplant, celery
Level 3: what do these ingredients have in common? Ox blood soup, lamb, silkworm pupae, oyster, skate
Answer: foods that split people sharply into #LoveItOrHateIt camps
Somehow, without really meaning to, today ended up being a #LoveItOrHateItBreakfast. Slice the celery thin with a knife and the cucumber thin with a mandoline. Top with mayonnaise and sprouts. Finish with a dressing of white wine vinegar, pepper, and a little salt. 
Would've been perfect if I'd chopped cilantro on top instead of the sprouts.

핑크페퍼-냉파-이거슨오늘아침의팩트.title: Pink Pepper, Fridge Cleanout: This Is This Morning's Fact
핑크페퍼-냉파-이거슨오늘아침의팩트.intro:
20201208, Even domestically, some media outlets have spread fear and misinformation about flu vaccines by spotlighting deaths that occurred after vaccination. Last fall, more than 100 people died within days of getting a flu shot, yet not a single case was found to be linked to the vaccine. When media outlets spread baseless suspicion and misinformation instead of verifying facts before reporting, it's hard not to feel pessimistic about the fight against fake news. (Koo Bon-kwon, 'Vaccine Scaremongering and Nonsense') 
Fake news speaks in storytelling; fact-checking answers with facts. That's probably exactly why fake news spreads so easily while the fact-checking that corrects it struggles to keep up. 
Grate the kohlrabi into thin strips. Slice the apple thin with a knife instead (grating turns apple mushy). Add radish sprouts and drizzle with a dressing of olive oil, sugar, salt, and lemon juice. A little pepper and #pinkpepper on top. Several days now of #fridgecleanout #ThisIsThisMorningsFact

폴렌타-유동식-아무튼폴렌타.title: Polenta, Anyway: A Soft Polenta Breakfast
폴렌타-유동식-아무튼폴렌타.intro:
20201207, On the other end of the phone, Tomoko keeps going. 'Boil water, put in the gochujang, then the pork, the pork belly...' 'Wait, why does tteokbokki need pork in it?' A conversation I had a long time ago with a junior colleague who'd learned to make tteokbokki from a book (no idea which book, but apparently the recipe really did call for pork). 
It's the same story for me (Jo-sik) with #polenta. All I really knew was that it's made from corn and that you just pour in water and boil it, roughly speaking — I'd never properly eaten it before, so every time I made it I wondered, 'is this actually what it's supposed to taste like?' As it happens, I stumbled onto a fairly detailed recipe on a blog last night. 
First, the mushrooms to go on top of the polenta. Melt butter in a pan, then sauté minced garlic followed by mushrooms. Once that looks about right, add a splash of balsamic and a little sugar and sauté a bit more. (Tasting it — sour, sweet, sort of both. Next time I'll just season it with salt instead.) 
Now, let's make the polenta I found on the blog. Add salt to boiling water and drizzle in a spoonful of olive oil. (Important! The ratio of polenta to water is 1:4.) Stir in the polenta powder, then add cheese. Just like last time, it comes together almost anticlimactically fast. Top with the mushrooms and a drizzle of olive oil, more cheese, and pepper. A wonderful #softfood. #PolentaAnyway 
*Reference: Naver blog, 'Rome's Palate, A Table Setting'

김용섭-언컨텍트-디지털전환.title: Kim Yong-sub's Uncontact: Digital Transformation Ricotta Salad
김용섭-언컨텍트-디지털전환.intro:
20201206, (Something I'd jotted down a while back) In 2018, Hyundai Card introduced RPA into its operations, and employee working hours dropped significantly while errors from simple mistakes also declined — a genuine improvement in the quality of work. RPA reportedly saved the company 15,628 work-hours a year, equivalent to the annual working hours of 70 employees. In other words, it was like gaining 70 extra workers for free. (Kim Yong-sub, Uncontact) #KimYongsub #Uncontact #RPA
A bit later than other companies, but we've now introduced RPA into my own work. It seems like the perfect tool for any area involving fixed, repetitive tasks, and it should genuinely cut down working hours. What we need to guard against, though, is letting it turn into headcount reduction — because the number-one premise behind the digital transformation we're pursuing has to be people. #DigitalTransformation #digitaltransformation #DigitalTransformation
So today: a very human ricotta cheese salad, standing up to the age of AI. Throw together whatever's left in the fridge — frisée, cucumber, green beans, cherry tomatoes, apple, celery — (thrown together, have you ever seen such a human recipe?), then scrape ricotta cheese all the way down with an ice cream scoop and drop it lightly on top. Scatter over the world's prettiest cranberries, long-soaked in Cuban rum, and some sliced almonds, roughly. For the dressing, balsamic, honey, lemon juice, olive oil, basil... except no basil on hand, so skip it — just toss it all together. Truly, a most human ricotta cheese.

바다거북수프를끓이자.title: Let's Cook Turtle Soup: Breakfast Requests Welcome
바다거북수프를끓이자.intro:
#breakfast Want me to make you one?
A daughter comes home upset because she worked up the courage to raise her hand and speak in class, but was only met with laughter. 
Her mother tells her, 
"Congratulations. That's another failure point in the bank."
She pats her daughter's small head. 
"Once you rack up enough failure points, you get to pick tonight's 
menu. I'll make you whatever you like."
Miyashita Natsu, Let's Cook Turtle Soup
If something bad happened to you today, 
and you've racked up a failure point of your own,
I thought that even though you can't actually taste it, 
just looking at a breakfast 
made exactly the way you want it might bring some comfort. 
Especially since, for most office workers, 
breakfast itself is already 
something you can barely dream of. 
Send me a DM with the breakfast you'd like.
Na Jo-sik will make it for you. 
E.g.) Please make carrot rapé!
Oh, and if you have a reference image, feel free to send that along too — 
after all, this will be a breakfast you eat with your eyes.

시저샐러드-조식-아침밥.title: Caesar Salad Breakfast
시저샐러드-조식-아침밥.intro:
20201205, July 4, 1924, at Caesar's restaurant in LA — running low on ingredients and worried about what to do, Caesar improvised a (invented on the spot) salad for his guests out of whatever was left, romaine and bread among it. It became an unexpected sensation and turned into the #CaesarSalad we still enjoy today. Made as close to the original recipe as possible, this Caesar salad is wonderfully simple and clean. 
-Drizzle olive oil in a pan and toast bread to make croutons. 
-Tear apart the world's prettiest romaine and plate it, then add olive oil, salt, pepper, lemon juice, 
-and top with parmigiano cheese and the croutons. 
Reference: Hwang Yu-jin's Organic - The Enzyme Table

뀰-꿀사과-꿀.title: Honey Tangerines, Honey Apples, Honey
뀰-꿀사과-꿀.intro:
20201204, Around this time every year, you can easily spot fruit-truck signs advertising "ggyul" (a portmanteau of tangerine + honey). Just how sweet do they have to be to earn that name? #ggyul And sitting right next to them, nine times out of ten, are #honeyapples. 
When you cut an apple open, that translucent patch inside we call "honey" is actually a physiological disorder called water core (or glassiness) — something you'd never find in an apple grown under normal conditions. 
I cut the apple open. No honey inside. A little disappointed, I julienne it anyway and soak it in honey water. Julienne the kohlrabi too, then plate the honey-water-soaked apple together with today's companion, kohlrabi, pour over a dressing of olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard, and finish with pepper.

라프레리-베타카로틴-당근.title: La Prairie Beta-Carotene Carrots
라프레리-베타카로틴-당근.intro:
20201203, Lotte's drink '2%' got jokes like 'tastes like peach-rinse water,' and a truffle potato chip with a mere 0.0000007% truffle oil content got roasted with 'you'd get more truffle eating the pig that dug it up.'
But the caviar in pricey skincare like #LaPrairie — marketed with claims that 'the mighty power of caviar gives strength to your skin' — sits at roughly that same trace level. And today's star, the carrot, said to be packed with beta-carotene that slows skin aging and supports eye health, actually contains only 8,300 micrograms per 100 grams — that is, a mere 0.0083 grams — of #betacarotene.
It brings to mind a tweet I once read: someone walked into a cafe, drank an iced Americano, felt the caffeine kick in and studied like mad, then on the way out noticed the receipt said 'Iced Americano (Decaf)' — and realized that whether your head spins fast or not has nothing to do with caffeine, it's all mindset. A morning that calls for that kind of receipt-based enlightenment. 
Slice the #carrot into nice pieces and pan-fry in olive oil. Arrange the carrot attractively, this way and that, then finish with Greek yogurt and a sprinkle of pepper.

김응준-그놈의소속감-그린샐러드.title: Kim Eung-jun, Sense of Belonging, Green Salad
김응준-그놈의소속감-그린샐러드.intro:
20201202, Even building a road in front of a high school draws opposition from someone. That road is obviously necessary for students commuting to and from school. And yet residents whose homes or shops would have to come down can't help but push back, and neighbors clash over which direction the road should even take. Civil servants have to work in situations where no one can say in a word which side truly serves the public interest. The public administration scholar Schubert once said that trying to define the public interest is like building a castle on sand. We toss around words like equality, fairness, and justice easily, but reality never lines up so neatly. A state of perfect justice or perfect equality is only possible in a dictatorship. (#KimEungJun, #ThatDamnSenseOfBelonging)
Someone once said: people's standard for 'fair' is usually whatever happens to work in their own favor. 
Romaine that's been waiting in the fridge for days, plus frisée, green beans, peas, celery, and cheese, stacked up with a modest dressing. A truly equal, fair, and just #greensalad. Everything here revolves around me, but that's fine — this is the dictatorship of the Breakfast Republic of Na-Josik, so it's more than possible.

연어스테이크-연어세비체-연어샐러드.title: Salmon Steak, Salmon Ceviche, Salmon Salad
연어스테이크-연어세비체-연어샐러드.intro:
20201201, The Joseon dynasty had three chief state councilors — Yeonguijeong, Jwauijeong, Uuijeong. The three-legged crow that appears in 'Jumong,' the show that made Song Il-gook a star (and, incidentally, the father of triplets), has exactly three legs. Slang like 'jimotmi' or 'sam-yeon-beong' tends to land on three syllables, and most Korean names — like Na. Jo. Sik. — are three syllables too. (A sudden pivot, I know, but) Hegel's dialectic is likewise built on the three of thesis-antithesis-synthesis. In short, three is the number of perfection. With #salmonsteak, #salmonceviche, and today's #salmonsalad, three days of salmon breakfasts complete the set. It is finished. 
I carefully lay down the last of the sprouts and the frisée still hanging around, then arrange cucumber, black olives, and salmon together in harmony. A little pepper and salt, then a dressing of olive oil, whole-grain mustard, and white wine vinegar.

리미트리스-파스닙-파스닙수프.title: Limitless Parsnip & Parsnip Soup
리미트리스-파스닙-파스닙수프.intro:
20201130, #Limitless (2012), starring Bradley Cooper, follows a man who stumbles onto a pill called NZT that lets him use 100% of his brain. 
The scene that stuck with me was the visual effect at the moment he swallows the pill — the moment a human brain switches to 100% — where a hologram-like double steps out of the protagonist and calmly looks back at him. That double felt like another self, standing one step back, able to see me objectively. I have no idea whether the filmmakers meant it that way. 
As always, more or less, it's a Monday morning commute with a busy mind — even more so with the year winding down. No NZT for me, but I hope this week too I can step back, look at myself objectively, and make the right calls. 
(Super-simple) Salmon Ceviche
-Dice the star of the show, the salmon, into bite-sized pieces. (The star has to make its own separate entrance.)
-Dice bell pepper, cucumber, tomato, and black olives to the same size as the salmon.
-Add the pre-cooked quinoa and the rest of the ingredients, then fold in the salmon and mix gently.
-Taste as you go, adding salt, pepper, and lemon juice, then finish with olive oil and toss well.
Parsnip Soup (made last night)
-In a pan, add butter, onion, and roughly chopped parsnip, and sauté.
-Add water and vegetable stock to the sautéed pan and bring to a boil.
-Purée finely with a hand blender. (Heavy cream would be nice here, but I didn't have any) Add a splash of milk and simmer.

향수-어느살인자의이야기-펜넬.title: Perfume, The Story of a Murderer, Fennel & Salmon
향수-어느살인자의이야기-펜넬.intro:
20201129, Something reminded me of #Perfume:TheStoryOfAMurderer, so I rewatched it a few weeks ago. The scent that drives the whole story — reeking fish, the stench of Paris's back alleys — felt like something I was smelling through my eyes. The premise, a man crafting the most beautiful, legendary scent in the world out of human beings, is deeply seductive. By the film's second half, since it's not a smell you can actually breathe in, that ultimate scent just kept circling in my head. One thing is clear: it's the scent of a person, not the kind of scent that comes out of a shower gel or a fine perfume. #Perfume #TheStoryOfAMurderer
It's nothing compared to that 'ultimate scent,' but #fennel has a distinctive aroma of its own. Supposedly that aroma cuts through the gaminess of meat and fish, which is how it earned the nickname #theherbformeat. 
 
-Sprinkle olive oil and salt over the #salmon and let it rest (pat pat). 
-Thinly slice the prettiest #fennel in the world and pan-fry both sides in olive oil. 
-Wake up the resting salmon and pan-fry it, carefully, carefully. 
-Plate the fennel and salmon together, add black olives, capers, and pink pepper, and finish with a crack of black pepper.

오늘의조식-브런치-어색.title: Frisée Salad (a Little Awkward Brunch)
오늘의조식-브런치-어색.intro:
20201128, #TodaysBreakfast (which, timing-wise, ended up being #brunch) is a frisée salad — except this is my first time with frisée, my first time poaching an egg, and I don't even really eat bacon, so the whole thing feels unfamiliar. I planned this breakfast during the week with real enthusiasm, but it turned into a combination of nothing but unfamiliar things, and maybe that's why both the taste and the plating feel #awkward. I think I've gotten used to things, that I know them to some degree, but honestly there's still so much I'm curious about, so much that's still unfamiliar. Some things need patient waiting, others need active effort. Anyway, today's frisée salad will probably be remembered for its #awkward flavor. 
Over the prettiest frisée in the world, I add crispy #bacon, toasted #walnuts, and a #poachedegg, then dress it with olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard. #friseesalad — apparently a favorite in France's Lyon region.

초안-브런치.title: First Draft Brunch
초안-브런치.intro:
20201127, Someone hands me a proposal, hesitating: “It's just a draft.” A draft, usually, is the first attempt at writing something before it's made official. Since it's the first version, you'd assume the Chinese character in the word for 'draft' means 'first' — but surprisingly, it's actually the character for 'grass.' So a draft, literally, is a plan that sways like grass. #draft
Let's remember that — you, me, all of us — we've all had moments of swaying in the wind like grass. So, truly, I'm rooting for you. 
Getting off work at dawn yesterday turned this from #breakfast into #brunch.

퀴노아-뿌리채소퀴노아샐러드.title: Root Vegetable Quinoa Salad
퀴노아-뿌리채소퀴노아샐러드.intro:
20201126, Hi, Elon! You've seen 'The Martian,' right? The one where Watney, stranded alone on Mars, manages to grow potatoes and eventually makes his way back to Earth after all sorts of trouble. I heard you're planning to actually send humans to Mars by 2025, so just in case, SpaceX is definitely going to need some famine-relief crops. 
I'd actually recommend sweet potatoes over regular potatoes. In terms of how many people a given area can feed, corn supports 1 person, wheat 1.6, rice 2.4 — but sweet potatoes support 3.9. On top of that, sweet potatoes grow well even in poor soil and are rich in antioxidants, fiber, and potassium, so they'd help with skin aging from Mars's harsh air, and also with the stress-eating that comes from an irregular schedule and homesickness for Earth. Take this recipe with you. 
I'm rushing out the door for work, so I'll keep this short. 
November 26, 2020 
Na-Josik
-Combine #quinoa and water at a 1:2 ratio, add a little olive oil and salt, and boil. 
-In a heated pan, toast sliced almonds, then pan-fry the sweet potato, then add olive oil and pan-fry the lotus root. 
-Plate the quinoa, sweet potato, and lotus root, then dress with olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard.
-Top with red onion, almonds, cilantro, parsley, and lots of pepper.

돌려깎고-쭈꾸미-오렌지쭈꾸미구이.title: Orange-Grilled Baby Octopus
돌려깎고-쭈꾸미-오렌지쭈꾸미구이.intro:
20201125, Baby Octopus No. 3 asked:
"No. 1, is it time for us to take over Earth now-zz?"
"No, not yet — we still need more time-zz."
No. 2 chimed in:
"But why? How much longer do we have to wait-zz?"
No. 1 stared at the ground and calmly continued:
"Starting next year, Earth time, humans will begin getting vaccinated against the coronavirus. We have to wait until then-zz."
No. 3 asked again:
"What does the coronavirus vaccine have to do with our conquest of Earth-zz?"
No. 1 answered in a determined voice:
"Listen closely, No. 2, No. 3. Once the vaccine comes out, humans will race to get it. But the vaccine contains a special something, shipped in from our home planet..."
At that exact moment, the shadow of an enormous fork fell over Octopus No. 1's head, and No. 1 never got to finish. 
Plating today's #breakfast turned out so different from what I'd pictured that I was still reeling from the shock, which is apparently why I started talking nonsense first thing in the morning. Still, it tastes incredible. 
Peel an orange in a spiral and lay it down as a bed. Warm a little olive oil in a pan with cracked pepper and a scattering of parsley, then blanch the thawed #babyoctopus. Finish with a dressing of olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard — #orangegrilledbabyoctopus, a great pairing for wine.

진양상가-세운상가-승효상.title: Jinyang & Sewoon Arcades, Seung H-Sang, Thai-Style Tamarind Egg
진양상가-세운상가-승효상.intro:
20201124, I once jotted down a note about a striking answer the former Seoul Metropolitan Government Chief City Architect gave to the question, “If you had 3 nights and 4 days to show a foreigner around Seoul, what would you show them?” His answer: Seoul's points, lines, and planes. 
In short — Seoul's points are its great buildings, like Gyeongdong Presbyterian Church; Seoul's lines are cross-sections of the city like #JinyangArcade and #SewoonArcade (and Jongmyo Shrine, which you reach at the end of that line); and Seoul's planes are its landscapes, like Bukhan Mountain and the Seoul City Wall. 
*This is from Jin Jung-kwon's 'Culture Tearoom,' the episode on architect Seung H-Sang, Part 1, around the 45:30 mark. 
COVID-19 has crushed the tourism industry, and — like that one airline's ad copy put it — travel has left us, even though it's we who need to leave on a trip. But whenever a time comes when we can travel freely and worry-free again, I'd love to gladly offer a Thai friend Seoul's points, lines, and planes. 
So today, thinking of a Thai friend who might visit Seoul someday, #ThaiStyleBreakfast #breakfast #tamarindegg
-Boil the eggs until soft-boiled and set aside. 
-Pour oil into a pan and lightly fry the outside of the eggs (ladling the hot oil over them with a spoon). 
-Dressing: tamarind (1), fish sauce (1), palm sugar (1), water (2).
-Top carefully with fried shallots and the prettiest, most fragrant #cilantro in the world, finely chopped.

사회적거리두기-콥샐러드.title: Social Distancing Cobb Salad
사회적거리두기-콥샐러드.intro:
20201123, According to a scholar named Hediger, animals too practice something like distancing, which can be sorted into flight distance, critical distance, personal distance, and social distance. The first two — flight and critical distance — come into play between individuals of different species, while personal and social distance can be observed between members of the same species. (Kim Hyun-jung, Science Times) 
The social distancing we've been hard-pressed to maintain has just been raised to Level 2. Even among the same species, it seems like we need to live for a while as if we should keep flight distance or critical distance, if we ever want to get back to a more humane, social distance later on. That feels especially true when I think of the small business owners whose livelihoods are directly threatened by the tightened restrictions. 
Lay down leafy greens, top with tofu, corn, cherry tomatoes, boiled egg, and green olives, then dress with yogurt (instead of a calorie-bomb ranch) for a #cobbsalad 
*The Cobb salad reportedly got its start in 1937 at the Brown Derby restaurant in Hollywood, LA, when owner-chef Robert Howard Cobb chopped up leftover ingredients during a busy dinner rush to make himself something to eat.

피처링-피처링특집-콜라비.title: Featuring Special: Kohlrabi Som Tam & Avocado Crostini
피처링-피처링특집-콜라비.intro:
20201122, #Featuring originally means a singer other than the main artist singing a specific part of a song, or playing an instrument on it — and it's also sometimes used deliberately, bringing in a hugely famous artist to feature on a track just to pull in that artist's fans. With the belief that swapping in an unexpected ingredient, when you don't have the one a dish is normally known for, can produce surprisingly unique results, today's breakfast is a #featuringspecial
Som Tam (feat. Kohlrabi)
1. Julienne the prettiest #kohlrabi in the world along with carrot, and prepare blanched #greenbeans. 
2. Combine palm sugar (1), fish sauce (1), lime juice (1) with 2-3 bird's eye chilies and tomato, and mash together. 
3. Toss the vegetables from step 1 with the mixture from step 2 and fried shallots. 
(Kohlrabi in place of green papaya, bird's eye chilies in place of Thai chili, fried shallots in place of dried shrimp)
Avocado Crostini (feat. Sweet Potato & Som Tam Dressing)
1. Heat olive oil in a pan and lightly pan-fry sweet potato slices on both sides. 
2. Top the sweet potato with tomato that's been marinated in the kohlrabi som tam dressing, 
3. Slice avocado on top, then finish with a light drizzle of som tam dressing
(Sweet potato in place of bread, som tam dressing in place of the usual olive oil/white wine vinegar dressing)

방울토마토-블랙올리브-옥수수.title: Cherry Tomato, Black Olive & Corn Salad
방울토마토-블랙올리브-옥수수.intro:
20201121, Heat olive oil in a pan and pan-fry the prettiest, tastiest #cherrytomatoes in the world. Cherry tomatoes really do get sweeter the more you cook them. Plate them with leafy greens, #blackolives, and #corn, then top with #greekyogurt. 
I tried to sort out my thoughts on 'Na-Josik' as an #alterego, but it wasn't coming together, so I set it aside for now. Got my #fluvaccine yesterday, so I'm feeling a bit #blah today.

중산층-거대한만두-계란오믈렛.title: The 'Giant Dumpling' Egg Omelette
중산층-거대한만두-계란오믈렛.intro:
20201120, The topic of the #middleclass came up over lunch at work yesterday, which sent me back to look up France's criteria for it. Here's what I found:
-Should speak at least one foreign language.
-Should actively play a sport.
-Should be able to play an instrument.
-Should be able to cook a dish with a flavor that's distinctly your own.
-Should take a firm stand against social injustice.
-Should volunteer regularly to help the vulnerable.
Comparing that to Korea's version of 'middle class,' I once again decided I really ought to move to France. 
Whisk two eggs, add a pinch of salt and pepper, pour into a pan over low heat, and tilt the pan to one side to shape it nicely — and before you know it, out comes an #eggomelette that looks just like a #giantdumpling, with 'a flavor and look distinctly its own,' which, conveniently, fits France's middle-class criteria perfectly. 
I'm not the least bit envious of the boring old #rugbyballshapedomelette anyone can make. T_T

카카오-구독경제-한겨레신문.title: Asparagus & Green Bean Salad
카카오-구독경제-한겨레신문.intro:
20201119, Starting the 19th, you can rent Winia Aid's Dimchae kimchi refrigerator through KakaoTalk. By the end of this year, you'll also be able to get Bodyfriend massage chairs, Amorepacific cosmetics, Winix air purifier filters, and Hanssem mattresses the same way. (...) “Existing companies never built a convenient subscription platform, but Kakao did,” the company said, adding that it plans to let people handle consultations, contracts, and payments — things that used to be clunky offline processes — with just a few clicks inside a KakaoTalk channel. They also said they plan to expand beyond products like appliances and consumables into recurring services like cleaning. (The Hankyoreh, ‘Kakao Builds a Wallet... Betting Big on a Convenient Subscription Platform’) #Kakao #subscriptioneconomy #TheHankyoreh #Kakao 
Kakao says it's expanding into the subscription economy. A subscription economy is one where, for a set fee, a provider periodically delivers whatever product or service the customer wants. For providers, subscriptions mean stable, recurring revenue; for users, it means affordable access to things they need regularly — so there's little reason for either side to object. And given how platforms work, it's only natural for Kakao to expand its business around its subscriber base, so there's no real reason to blame them for that. But Kakao needs to remember just how heavy a responsibility it carries toward its 45 million KakaoTalk users — and their personal data. Shouldn't it, like Google once did, declare its own 'Don't be evil in Korea'? 
Heat olive oil in a pan with a little salt and pepper, and blanch the #asparagus and #greenbean. Top with #boiledegg, #pistachios, and #pepper, then dress with olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard 
#breakfast #morningmeal #salad #breakfast #salad #asparagus #greenbean #asparagusgreenbeansalad — an adaptation of my #myfrenchstylesalad recipe

집콕-달고나라떼-수플레오믈렛.title: Egg Bread & Microwave Tomato Soup
집콕-달고나라떼-수플레오믈렛.intro:
20201118, With COVID-19 dragging on and working from home and #stayingin becoming the norm, all kinds of dishes that never used to exist are popping up. There's a whole genre of 'stir it N times' recipes — #dalgonalatte (stir 1,000 times), #souffleomelette (also 1,000 times), #maplesyrupjam (500 times), and the like. 
#easycooking, or what some call #hackcooking, is having a moment again too — things like microwave #tomatosoup, #brownies, and #lasagna. For anyone short on ingredients or kitchen tools, or who just finds cooking hard for whatever reason, this seems like a great way to get one satisfying meal. Though if COVID keeps going like this, maybe someday these microwave hacks will get the same respectful treatment as the #Eumsikdimibang. 
*Eumsikdimibang: Korea's oldest known Hangul cookbook, written roughly 400 years ago by Lady Jang of Andong, containing 146 recipes.
Egg Bread
1. Mix pancake mix and water at a 2:1 ratio, add a pinch of salt. 
2. Pour the batter into a mug, then crack an egg on top. 
3. Microwave for 3 minutes. 
4. Around the 2:30 mark, listen for a pop. The yolk bursts and sets off a chain reaction that makes the egg bread explode. Plate whatever egg bread survives the explosion. 
Tomato Soup
1. Cut the tomato in half. 
2. Add 5 spoonfuls of water
3. Sprinkle with a little butter, salt, and pepper. 
(Olive oil works instead of butter, though butter gives it a slightly more refined flavor)
5. Microwave for 3 minutes.

어쩌다어른-김지윤-A형.title: Radish, Pistachio & Radish Sprout Salad
어쩌다어른-김지윤-A형.intro:
20201117, There was a time when people were judged by blood type — Type A is timid, Type B is wild, that sort of thing. These days MBTI is having its moment instead. It sorts human personalities into 16 types, so it's probably a bit better at capturing individual traits than blood type. (Oh, and now that I think of it, there was also that thing about personality-by-favorite-snack.)
A couple of days ago, while flipping through YouTube, I watched an interesting video about personality traits by birth order. First-borns, apparently, tend to represent responsibility, worry, control, and diligence. Second children, raised in a tug-of-war between an older and younger sibling, tend to have experienced confusion, competition, and unfairness. The youngest is usually the most doted-on, but supposedly struggles a bit with decision-making. And only children tend to be relaxed about most things and have trouble maintaining close relationships, but score high academically. 
#SuddenlyGrownUp #KimJiYoon “The Most Common Traits of First-Borns, Second Children, Youngests, and Only Children”
Like blood type or MBTI, it's hard to sort humans into a handful of neat categories. So there's no reason — or need — to take it as gospel, but it really does help to understand where someone around you is coming from, and to build common ground by talking it through. In some future where forming human relationships has become difficult for whatever reason, maybe we'll all end up printing #TypeA #INFJ #OnlyChild #SnackPersonalityAce on our business cards, just to speed up making a connection. (Imagining this alone on the subway on my way to work, shoulders shaking with laughter, ha ha ha.)
Today it's another #inseasonspecial: slice #radish and pan-fry it lightly in olive oil. A light dressing of olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard, topped with #pistachios and #radishsprouts for an instant #upscaleupgrade.

루시드폴-콜라비콘체르토-제주구좌당근.title: Lucid Fall's Kohlrabi Concerto, Jeju Gujwa Carrot Salad
루시드폴-콜라비콘체르토-제주구좌당근.intro:
20201116, Today's main ingredient is kohlrabi, which pairs nicely with Lucid Fall's 'Kohlrabi Concerto.' The song was literally sung and performed by Lucid Fall's dog, Bohyeon — he recorded the sound Bohyeon makes chewing on kohlrabi, then used granular synthesis to vary the tempo and pitch and turned it into a full song. 
'Granular synthesis' sounds technical, but really it just means recording a short sound and, with a whole lot of love for Bohyeon, dressing it up into something that passes for music. #LucidFall #KohlrabiConcerto
A few days ago I was talking with a coworker about seasonal produce, and it turns out apples and kohlrabi are in season (November-December), so I grabbed some right away. #JejuGujwaCarrot season is coming soon too. I can't wait. 
Julienne the #apple and #kohlrabi and toss with a fragrant dressing of olive oil, white wine vinegar, and whole-grain mustard, plus chopped parsley. Finish with a good squeeze of lemon juice.

유니클로질샌더대란-닭가슴살-아스파라거스.title: Chicken Breast & Asparagus Salad
유니클로질샌더대란-닭가슴살-아스파라거스.intro:
20201115, A junior colleague shared a post captioned 'Full of Traitors,' about the #UniqloJilSanderFrenzy. This isn't the first Uniqlo x Jil Sander collaboration as far as I know, but this round probably launched a wider, better range of pieces. In an interview on Uniqlo's website, when asked how the natural landscape of northern Germany influenced him and his design, Jil Sander answered this way: 
“This area is known for its clear, bright sunlight. The light is so pure that everything is illuminated right down to the detail. That light is an extremely important factor for me in choosing fabric, because it's closely tied not just to color but to the quality of the material itself. Under this light, there's no faking it — every detail of the weave is laid bare. That's how you can pick out only the very best fabric.” (Jil Sander, Uniqlo website)
I remember reading once that Italy's brilliant sunlight accounted for 80% of what let sculptors create masterpieces like the Pietà or David. Under that kind of light, the curves of a sculpture and the shadows they cast would have stood out all the more. Light that reveals the detail of a weave, light that maximizes the shadow of a sculpture — it's all light. 
The breakfast photos I make and shoot every morning are also heavily shaped by light. Thanks to that, I've really come to feel the light of summer, fall, and winter. Now that we're deep into late fall heading into early winter, I usually make and photograph breakfast before sunrise, so I'm always missing natural light. In that sense, weekends are a relief. It feels like this season's light doesn't have much time left either. So, #Carpe_Diem
Season #chickenbreast with salt, pepper, and olive oil, then pan-fry. Trim the prettiest, most lovable #asparagus in the world, season with a little salt, and pan-fry. Top the chicken breast with the asparagus and #parmigiano cheese, and finish with thin shredded red chili threads
#breakfast #morningmeal #salad #chickenbreastasparagussalad #breakfast #salad #chickenwithasparagus #asparagus — adapted from my #myfrenchstylesalad recipe, originally made with beef tenderloin and aralia shoots

그레이리스트-찐리스트-독차지.title: Grey List, Real Favorites, All Mine: Ricotta-Stuffed Chicken Breast
그레이리스트-찐리스트-독차지.intro:
20201114, The restaurants that make it onto a 'grey list' are, perfectly, the 'good enough' places — spots you can recommend without much thought, that won't get you side-eyed, and that wouldn't feel like a loss even if they suddenly became wildly famous. They're also the kind of places food writers can happily return to for the tenth time on assignment, even after they've already eaten there plenty of times off the clock. (Michael Booth, on food writers who never reveal their real favorite spots) #greylist
There's a 'grey list' you can hand out freely when someone asks for a good restaurant, and there's also a #realfavoriteslist you'd never share with anyone. Places like: a café around lunchtime with sunlight pouring through the window, a spot that somehow serves everything — rice, noodles, drinks, even sashimi — a quiet convenience store, a pub you stumble on at the end of a summer night's walk. Places I want to #keepallformyself, forever. What's on your real favorites list?
Season #chickenbreast with salt, pepper, and olive oil, slice it partway open, and pan-fry. Whip #ricottacheese with parsley and pepper and stuff it into the pocket. Wash the prettiest romaine in the world thoroughly, plate it, and finish with #gradapadanocheese, #toastedwalnuts, and a squeeze of lime.

적채-스테이크.title: Red Cabbage Steak
적채-스테이크.intro:
20201113, An unplanned drink
only when I want to be comforted
I go looking for someone,
and pretend it's them I'm comforting.
(Choi Young-mi, Things That Never Come Back Again) 
Drink in moderation. 
Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté red onion, garlic, and the prettiest #redcabbage in the world. Top with a dressing of olive oil, whole-grain mustard, and white wine vinegar, and finish with cilantro.

다시만난세계-다만세-뱅뱅뱅.title: Into a New World, Bang Bang Bang: Melogold Som Sa Op
다시만난세계-다만세-뱅뱅뱅.intro:

Apparently, in the protests that followed — the 6th People's Grand March denouncing the Park Geun-hye/Choi Soon-sil scandal, and the Gwanghwamun candlelight vigils after that — you could quite often hear #IntoANewWorld and #BangBangBang too. 
At Bangkok's #PrideParade, held just the other day, I heard #BlackPink songs playing. I don't know which song it was, but it made me think first about the context of the lyrics versus the message of the event — which, hm, does that make me an #outoftoucholdtimer?

바다거북수프를끓이자-씨앗-생명.title: Let's Make Turtle Soup: Bean, Cucumber & Broccoli Salad
바다거북수프를끓이자-씨앗-생명.intro:
20201111, "They're kidney beans. Plant them in the soil when you get home — they'll sprout." 
The old man laughed, but I couldn't. Plant it in soil and it sprouts. I'd never thought about it that way before. This bean is alive. A living bean that is both seed and life. Suddenly, eating it felt frightening. (Miyashita Natsu, #LetsMakeTurtleSoup)
It's easy to forget that life exists in almost every ingredient we eat. This morning, kidney beans, chickpeas, tiger beans, peas, and black beans — so many #seeds and #lives — filled my hungry stomach.

정희진-융합-토마토샐러드.title: Jung Hee-jin's Convergence Tomato Salad
정희진-융합-토마토샐러드.intro:
20201110, One opposite of convergence is grand theory. A self built on grand theory insists it can explain everything. But what a batter stepping into the strike zone actually needs to know isn't 'the history of world professional baseball' — it's the opposing pitcher's throwing pattern, his expression, the pitch he just threw. Life is a string of small units just like that. Related sayings: 'God is in the details,' 'live in the present,' 'situation,' 'context.' (Jung Hee-jin, The Human World Is Small: The Strike Zone) #JungHeeJin #convergence
Considering that the original meaning of #CarpeDiem leans less toward 'try hard' and more toward 'enjoy the moment,' and that today's patience and sacrifice never guarantee a rosy future anyway, it seems better to put effort into the small, moment-to-moment 'present me' rather than clinging to some grand past-and-future self. (Honestly, that's what I'm already doing.) In the end, maybe the 'present me' is simply the sum of the past me and the future me — the one carrying my hopes for what's ahead. 
Lay down the big tomatoes, then top with the small ones. A little olive oil and balsamic, plus parsley and pepper for a different kind of flavor #tomatosalad #breakfast #morningmeal #salad #breakfast #salad #tomatosalad

고시-삼치-아보카도.intro:
